Start with minimal pressure — your forearms should bear most of your weight. | Take a slow, deep inhale through the nose, allowing your belly to expand downward into the ball. You should feel the ball press back against the tissue as your diaphragm descends. | זרום אויר לחלוטין ובאיטיות דרך שפות סגורות, מאפשר לגופך להירגע עוד יותר אל הכדור תוך כדי הנשימה. הרקמה מתחת לכדור צריכה להרכך מעט עם כל זרימת אויר. | Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, until you notice a reduction in tension or discomfort at that spot. | Slowly shift your torso a short distance — about one inch — in any direction to move the ball to an adjacent area, then repeat the breathing cycle. | Work across the lower ribcage on that side, covering the area from just left of the sternum to the outer edge of the ribcage, spending 20–30 seconds at each point. | דחוף את עצמך בזהירות מהכדור, סדר מחדש אותו לצד השני של קו האמצע, וחזור על כל הרצף. | סיים בהתגלגלות על הגב ושלוש-חמש נשימות סרעפתיות איטיות ומלאות כדי לאפשר לרקמה להתייצב.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and sit beside it, then carefully lower yourself so the ball sits just to one side of your spine in the lower back, not directly on the vertebrae. | Lean your body weight into the ball by supporting yourself on your hands or forearms and bending your knees with feet flat on the floor. | Breathe out and allow your muscles to relax into the pressure of the ball. | Slowly shift your body up and down a few centimeters to roll the ball along the erector spinae from the top of the hip toward the mid-back. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension softens. | Continue rolling and pausing on any additional tight areas along the same side of the spine. | When finished with one side, carefully roll off the ball, reposition it to the opposite side of the spine, and repeat. | Finish by moving gently off the ball, resting flat on your back for a moment before standing.
tRu: Положите роликовый мяч на пол и сядьте рядом с ним, затем осторожно опустите себя, чтобы мяч находился с одной стороны позвоночника в нижней части спины, не прямо на позвонках. | Перенесите вес тела на мяч, опираясь на руки или предплечья и сгибая колени, стопы прижаты к полу. | Выдыхайте и плавно углубляйте растяжку, слегка продвигая таз вперед и вниз, не прогибая поясницу. | Slowly shift your body up and down a few centimeters to roll the ball along the erector spinae from the top of the hip toward the mid-back. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension softens. | Продолжайте кататься и задерживаться на любых дополнительных напряжённых участках вдоль той же стороны позвоночника. | When finished with one side, carefully roll off the ball, reposition it to the opposite side of the spine, and repeat. | Завершите, плавно сойдя с мяча, полежав на спине мгновение перед тем, как встать.
tHe: Place a rollball on the floor and sit beside it, then carefully lower yourself so the ball sits just to one side of your spine in the lower back, not directly on the vertebrae. | Lean your body weight into the ball by supporting yourself on your hands or forearms and bending your knees with feet flat on the floor. | נשור ואפשר לשרירים שלך להירגע אל לחץ הכדור. | Slowly shift your body up and down a few centimeters to roll the ball along the erector spinae from the top of the hip toward the mid-back. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension softens. | המשך ללחוץ ולהישאר על כל אזורים נוספים צמודים לאותו צד של החוטש. | When finished with one side, carefully roll off the ball, reposition it to the opposite side of the spine, and repeat. | סיים בהזזה עדינה מהכדור, מנוחה על הגב למשך רגע לפני הקימה.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and kneel or sit beside it so the ball sits next to your hip on the side you want to stretch. | Lower your body sideways and position the rollball under your lateral waist, just above the hip bone where the external oblique runs. | Support your upper body with your bottom forearm on the floor, keeping your elbow directly beneath your shoulder. | Extend your legs out so your body forms a straight line from head to feet, stacking your feet or resting the lower knee on the floor for stability. | Relax the side of your waist into the ball and let gravity apply gentle pressure to the tissue. | Breathe slowly and deeply, allowing the muscles to soften with each exhale. | Slowly roll the ball a few centimeters forward and back along the lateral waist to find and dwell on tight spots. | Hold on any tender area for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tissue release. | Repeat on the opposite side, spending equal time on each.
tRu: Положите массажный мяч на пол и встаньте на колени или сядьте рядом с ним так, чтобы мяч находился рядом с бедром с той стороны, которую вы хотите растянуть. | Опустите тело вбок и расположите роликовый мяч под боковой талией, чуть выше костей таза, где проходит наружная косая мышца. | Support your upper body with your bottom forearm on the floor, keeping your elbow directly beneath your shoulder. | Вытяните ноги вместе, чтобы тело образовывало прямую линию от головы до стоп, поставив стопы одну на другую или опустив колено на пол для стабильности. | Relax the side of your waist into the ball and let gravity apply gentle pressure to the tissue. | Дышите медленно и глубоко, позволяя мышцам-сгибателям бедра еще больше расслабляться с каждым выдохом. Удерживайте растяжку в течение 20–30 секунд. | Slowly roll the ball a few centimeters forward and back along the lateral waist to find and dwell on tight spots. | Удерживайте на любой чувствительной точке 20–30 секунд, пока не почувствуете, как ткани расслабляются. | Repeat on the opposite side, spending equal time on each.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and stand or sit in a stable position near a wall or chair for balance. | Position the ball under the heel of one foot, keeping the opposite foot flat on the floor. | Shift enough weight onto the working foot to create comfortable but firm pressure on the ball. | Slowly roll the ball forward along the arch toward the ball of the foot, moving in a controlled, deliberate pace. | Pause on any tender or tight spots for 5–10 seconds to allow the tissue to release. | Continue rolling back toward the heel, sweeping the full length of the plantar fascia. | Angle the foot slightly inward, then outward, to cover the medial and lateral edges of the arch. | Perform 60–90 seconds of rolling on each foot, then switch sides.
tRu: Положите роликовый мяч на пол и встаньте или сядьте в устойчивом положении рядом со стеной или стулом для равновесия. | Position the ball under the heel of one foot, keeping the opposite foot flat on the floor. | Shift enough weight onto the working foot to create comfortable but firm pressure on the ball. | Slowly roll the ball forward along the arch toward the ball of the foot, moving in a controlled, deliberate pace. | Пауза на любой болезненной или напряжённой точке на 5–10 секунд, чтобы позволить тканям расслабиться. | Продолжайте кататься к пятке, прорабатывая всю длину подошвенной фасции. | Наклоняйте стопу слегка внутрь, затем наружу, чтобы проработать внутренний и внешний края свода. | Выполняйте 60–90 секунд роллинга на каждой стопе, затем поменяйте стороны.

t: Sit at a table or desk with your forearm resting palm-down on the surface. Place the rollball on top of the dorsal (back) side of your forearm, roughly halfway between the wrist and elbow. | Rest your opposite hand on top of the ball to control pressure. Your forearm stays flat and relaxed on the surface throughout. | Apply moderate downward pressure through your top hand so the ball presses into the forearm extensor muscles. You should feel pressure without sharp or radiating pain. | Slowly roll the ball toward your elbow, moving at roughly one inch per second along the extensor muscle belly. Keep the movement controlled and deliberate. | When you find a tender or dense spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily, until the tension begins to ease. | Continue rolling back toward the wrist, covering the full length of the extensor compartment from just above the wrist crease to just below the lateral epicondyle (the bony point on the outside of the elbow). | Avoid rolling directly over the lateral epicondyle — stop approximately one finger-width before that bony landmark. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on each forearm, then switch sides and repeat. | Finish with 3–5 slow wrist circles in each direction to encourage circulation through the tissue.

t: Sit at a table or bench and place the rollball on the surface in front of you. | Rest your forearm on the table with the palm facing up, so the underside of your forearm (the flexor side) is exposed. | Position the rollball under your forearm, starting just above the wrist crease where the flexor tendons gather. | Apply gentle downward pressure through your forearm onto the ball, using your opposite hand on top of your forearm to add load as needed. | Slowly roll your forearm forward over the ball, moving from the wrist toward the elbow at a rate of roughly one inch per second. | When you encounter a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly, until the tension begins to ease. | Continue rolling up toward the mid-forearm, covering the full length of the flexor muscle belly. | Rotate your forearm slightly inward or outward to shift the ball onto adjacent flexor muscles and ensure full coverage. | Spend 60–90 seconds on each forearm, then switch arms and repeat.

nH: שחרור מסובב האמה פנימה עם כדור
t: Sit at a table or bench. Place the rollball on the surface and rest your forearm on top of it, palm facing down, so the ball sits against the inner forearm roughly halfway between the wrist and the elbow. | Apply gentle downward pressure through your forearm to compress the tissue against the ball. Use your free hand on top of your forearm to add extra load if needed. | Slowly roll the ball along the length of the inner forearm, moving from just above the wrist toward the elbow crease. Keep the motion controlled — about one inch per second. | When you reach a spot that feels notably tight or tender, pause and hold steady pressure there for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly until the tension softens. | Continue rolling back toward the wrist, covering the full length of the pronator muscle belly. | To increase specificity, rotate your palm slightly upward (supination) while holding on a tight spot. This places a mild active stretch on the pronator fibers under compression. | Spend 60–90 seconds working along the forearm, targeting the area along the medial (inner) edge from the wrist to just below the inner elbow. | Switch arms and repeat the same sequence on the opposite forearm.

t: Place a small, firm ball on a table or flat surface and sit or stand beside it. | Rest your forearm on the ball, positioning it on the lateral (outer) side of the forearm just below the elbow crease where the supinator muscle lies. | Allow your body weight to sink gently into the ball, creating moderate pressure on the tissue. | Slowly rotate your forearm from a palm-down (pronated) to a palm-up (supinated) position while maintaining pressure on the ball. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold that position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly. | Resume rolling by shifting your forearm slightly toward the wrist or elbow to explore adjacent tissue. | Continue for 60–90 seconds on each arm, adjusting ball position to cover the full supinator region. | Finish by gently shaking out your forearm and performing a light supination stretch to reinforce the release.

t: Sit on the floor and place the rollball on the ground beside your right hip. Lower your outer right hip onto the ball, positioning it just below and behind the bony crest of the ilium — roughly where the side seam of your shorts sits. | Support your upper body by placing your right hand on the floor behind you and your left hand in front for balance. Bend both knees and keep your feet flat on the floor. | Shift enough body weight onto the ball so you feel moderate pressure in the outer hip tissue, but not sharp or shooting pain. | Slowly move your hips in small, controlled circles or inch forward and backward to scan for areas of increased tension in the gluteus medius. | When you find a tender or tight spot, stop moving and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and letting the muscle relax into the ball. | After the tension in that spot decreases, continue scanning to find the next area of restriction, working from the posterior edge of the muscle toward the front of the hip. | To reach the anterior portion of the gluteus medius, rotate your hip slightly inward so the ball shifts toward the front of the outer hip. | Spend 60–90 seconds total on the right side, then reposition and repeat on the left hip.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and lie face-down, positioning the ball just inside the front of one hip bone (iliac crest), roughly an inch medial to the ASIS and low on the lower abdomen. | Lower yourself gently onto the ball so it contacts the soft tissue of the lower abdomen where the iliacus lies beneath, keeping most body weight through your forearms and opposite hip. | Breathe slowly and allow your abdomen to relax so the ball can sink progressively deeper toward the iliacus rather than pressing against braced abdominal muscles. | Scan for a tender or tight spot by making small, deliberate shifts of body weight — forward, back, or slightly side-to-side — until you locate a point of significant tension. | Hold sustained pressure on that tender point for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply and letting the tissue soften under the ball. | Once the initial tenderness eases, slowly flex and extend the same-side hip by sliding the knee out and back, using the movement to further release the iliacus against the ball. | Continue for a total of 60–90 seconds per side, repositioning the ball slightly to address different portions of the muscle. | When finished, press up slowly, rest a moment, then switch to the opposite side.
tRu: Положите роликовый мяч на пол и лягте на живот, расположив мяч чуть внутри переднего края одной подвздошной кости (iliac crest), примерно на дюйм медиальнее ASIS и низко на нижней части живота. | Опуститесь мягко на мяч так, чтобы он касался мягких тканей нижней живота, где подвздошная мышца находится под ней, удерживая большую часть веса тела на предплечьях и противоположном бедре. | Дышите медленно и позвольте вашему телу расслабиться под давлением. Избегайте напряжения в тазу — позвольте гравитации сделать работу. | Scan for a tender or tight spot by making small, deliberate shifts of body weight — forward, back, or slightly side-to-side — until you locate a point of significant tension. | Держите постоянное давление на эту болезненную точку в течение 20–30 секунд, глубоко дыша и позволяя ткани смягчиться под шариком. | Как только первоначальная болезненность утихнет, медленно сгибайте и разгибайте тазобедренный сустав той же стороны, сдвигая колено в сторону и обратно, используя движение для дополнительного расслабления подвздошно-поясничной мышцы о мяч. | Продолжайте в общей сложности 60–90 секунд на каждую сторону, немного изменяя положение мяча, чтобы проработать разные части мышцы. | When finished, press up slowly, rest a moment, then switch to the opposite side.

t: Lie face down on a firm surface with the rollball placed on the floor in front of you. | Position the ball just medial to your hip flexor crease — roughly two to three finger-widths inside and below the front of your hip bone (ASIS), where the iliopsoas runs toward the lesser trochanter. | Lower your body so the ball contacts the soft tissue of the hip flexor. Support your upper body on your forearms, keeping your spine neutral and your neck long. | Shift your weight slowly onto the ball until you feel moderate pressure on the target tissue. You are looking for a sensation of deep tension or mild discomfort — not sharp or nerve-like pain. | When you locate a tender or dense area, hold still on that spot and breathe steadily for 20–30 seconds. t: Place a rollball on the floor and lie on your back, bending your knees so your feet are flat on the floor. | Lift your head, position the ball at the base of your skull — roughly at the junction between your neck and the back of your head — and slowly lower your head onto it. | Allow the natural weight of your head to sink into the ball; do not press down forcefully. | Breathe slowly and let the surrounding muscles relax for 20–30 seconds as the initial tension begins to ease. | Make micro-adjustments by gently nodding your chin toward your chest or rotating your head a few degrees left or right to find tender spots. | When you locate a point of increased sensitivity, hold steady and breathe into the discomfort until you feel it soften — typically 20–45 seconds. | Reposition the ball slightly and repeat on any additional tight spots within the same region. | To finish, use both hands to support your head, lift it off the ball, and set the ball aside before lowering your head gently to the floor. | Rest for a moment, then slowly roll to one side before rising to avoid sudden head movement.
tRu: Положите роликовый мяч на пол и лягте на спину, согнув колени, чтобы ступни были flat на полу. | Поднимите голову, поместите мяч у основания черепа — примерно на стыке шеи и затылка — и медленно опустите голову на него. | Позвольте естественному весу головы лечь на мяч, не давите вниз с силой. | Дышите медленно и расслабляйтесь глубже в приседании с каждым выдохом, стремясь к комфортной конечной позиции. | Делайте микрорегулировки, слегка наклоняя подбородок к груди или поворачивая голову на несколько градусов влево или вправо, чтобы найти болезненные точки. | When you locate a point of increased sensitivity, hold steady and breathe into the discomfort until you feel it soften — typically 20–45 seconds. | Reposition the ball slightly and repeat on any additional tight spots within the same region. | To finish, use both hands to support your head, lift it off the ball, and set the ball aside before lowering your head gently to the floor. | Rest for a moment, then slowly roll to one side before rising to avoid sudden head movement.

t: Stand facing a wall or lie face down on the floor — both positions work. If standing, place the rollball between your upper chest (just below the collarbone) and the wall at chest height. | Position the ball on the clavicular portion of the pectoralis major: approximately one to two inches below the center of your collarbone, just medial to the shoulder. | Lean your body weight gently into the ball so it compresses the upper chest tissue. Start with light pressure to assess sensitivity before adding more load. | Slowly roll the ball in small circles or short strokes along the upper chest, moving from the sternum outward toward the front of the shoulder, staying below the collarbone the entire time. | When you locate a tender or tight spot, stop rolling and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly and allow the tissue to relax under the pressure. | After the hold, continue rolling laterally toward the front of the shoulder, covering the full width of the clavicular head. | To increase pressure, shift more body weight into the wall or floor. To reduce it, step slightly back or prop yourself up more with your free arm. | Spend 60–90 seconds working through the upper chest on one side, then switch to the other side and repeat. | Finish by gently retracting your shoulder blades and taking two or three slow, full breaths to help the chest open up.

t: Stand facing a wall or lie face down on the floor. If standing, place the rollball between your chest and the wall at approximately mid-chest height, with your arm relaxed at your side. | Begin at the sternal head: position the ball just lateral to the sternum, roughly at nipple height, so it sits on the broad, flat portion of the lower and mid chest. | Lean your body weight gently into the ball to create moderate compression. Start with light pressure and add load gradually as the tissue warms up. | Slowly roll the ball outward in short strokes, moving from the sternum toward the front of the shoulder and covering the full width of the sternal head. Spend about 30–45 seconds on this region. | Shift the ball upward toward the clavicular head: reposition it to approximately one to two inches below the collarbone, staying well clear of the bone itself. | Roll along the upper chest in the same outward direction — from the sternum toward the front of the shoulder — to work through the clavicular fibers. Spend another 30–45 seconds here. | Whenever you locate a tender or tight spot anywhere on the chest, stop rolling and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly and let the tissue relax under the pressure. | To modulate intensity, shift more body weight into the wall to increase pressure, or step slightly back to reduce it. Use your free hand to guide the ball and maintain control. | After completing both regions on one side, switch to the opposite side and repeat the full sequence. Finish each side with two or three slow, full breaths to encourage the chest to open.

nH: שחרור שרירי השוק הצדדיים עם כדור
t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the rollball on the ground just below your right knee on the outer side of the lower leg. | Position the lateral calf — the area over the peroneal muscles — directly on top of the rollball, using your hands behind you for support. | Lift your hips slightly off the floor so your body weight presses your lower leg into the rollball. | Slowly roll the ball down the outer lower leg toward the ankle, moving about 2–3 centimetres per breath. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold light pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension begins to release. | Continue rolling down to just above the outer ankle bone, then reverse direction and roll back up toward the knee. | Keep your upper body relaxed and breathe steadily throughout; avoid holding your breath. | Complete 2–3 passes along the peroneal muscles, then switch to the other leg and repeat.
tRu: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the rollball on the ground just below your right knee on the outer side of the lower leg. | Position the lateral calf — the area over the peroneal muscles — directly on top of the rollball, using your hands behind you for support. | Поднимите таз немного с пола, чтобы вес тела давил на голень, прижимая ее к роликовому мячу. | Slowly roll the ball down the outer lower leg toward the ankle, moving about 2–3 centimetres per breath. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold light pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until the tension begins to release. | Продолжайте кататься вниз к области чуть выше наружной лодыжки, затем смените направление и катайтесь обратно к колену. | Держите верхнюю часть тела расслабленной и дышите ровно на протяжении всего движения; не задерживайте дыхание. | Выполните 2–3 прохода вдоль малоберцовых мышц, затем перейдите на другую ногу и повторите.

t: Place a massage or lacrosse ball on the floor and sit on it, positioning the ball beneath one glute close to the center of the buttock where the piriformis lies. | Cross the ankle of the working leg over the opposite knee to open the hip and bring the piriformis closer to the surface. | Lean slightly toward the working side, shifting your body weight onto the ball to increase pressure. | Support yourself with both hands on the floor behind you and keep the non-working foot flat on the floor for balance. | Slowly roll your hips in small circles or forward and backward, exploring the area for tight or tender spots. | When you find a tender point, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 20 to 30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | Continue rolling and pausing across the full area of the piriformis for 60 to 90 seconds. | Gently lift off the ball, switch sides, and repeat the process on the opposite hip.
tRu: Положите массажный или лакроссовый мяч на пол и сядьте на него, расположив мяч под одной ягодицей близко к центру ягодиц, где находится грушевидная мышца. | Перекрестите лодыжку рабочей ноги над коленом противоположной, чтобы раскрыть таз и приблизить грушевидную мышцу к поверхности. | Слегка наклонитесь в сторону рабочей ноги, перенося вес тела на мяч для увеличения давления. | Support yourself with both hands on the floor behind you and keep the non-working foot flat on the floor for balance. | Slowly roll your hips in small circles or forward and backward, exploring the area for tight or tender spots. | When you find a tender point, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 20 to 30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | Продолжайте кататься и задерживаться на всей области грушевидной мышцы в течение 60–90 секунд. | Плавно оторвитесь от мяча, смените сторону и повторите процесс на противоположной стороне.
tHe: Place a massage or lacrosse ball on the floor and sit on it, positioning the ball beneath one glute close to the center of the buttock where the piriformis lies. | חצה את קרסול הרגל הפעילה מעל הברך הנגדית כדי לפתוח את הירך ולהביא את הפיריפורמיס קרוב יותר לפני השטח. | Lean slightly toward the working side, shifting your body weight onto the ball to increase pressure. | Support yourself with both hands on the floor behind you and keep the non-working foot flat on the floor for balance. | Slowly roll your hips in small circles or forward and backward, exploring the area for tight or tender spots. | When you find a tender point, pause and hold steady pressure on it for 20 to 30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | המשך ללחוץ ולהישאר על כל אזור הפיריפורמיס ל־60 עד 90 שניות. | הרם בעדינות מהכדור, החלף צד וחזור על התהליך באגן הנגדי.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat. Place the rollball beneath one glute, positioning it near the center of the buttock to target the gluteus maximus. | Shift your body weight onto the rollball by leaning back slightly and supporting yourself with your hands on the floor behind you. | Cross the ankle of the working leg over the opposite knee to open up the hip and increase access to the deeper gluteal tissue. | Using your hands and supporting foot, slowly roll the ball in small circles or short back-and-forth strokes across the gluteus maximus, scanning for areas of tension. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it and hold steady pressure for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly to allow the tissue to release. | Shift the rollball slightly toward the outer hip to address the gluteus medius, applying the same slow, deliberate rolling and pausing technique. | Continue working through the glute area for 60–90 seconds total, then gently lift your body off the rollball. | Switch sides and repeat the entire sequence on the opposite glute.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Place the rollball beneath your right glute, roughly in the center of the hip area where the piriformis sits. | Cross your right ankle over your left knee so the right leg forms a figure-four shape. This position opens the hip and increases pressure on the piriformis. | Place both hands on the floor behind you for support and lean your bodyweight slightly toward the right side to increase contact with the rollball. | Lift your left foot off the floor slightly to shift more of your weight onto the ball, then find a tender spot in the deep hip tissue. | Hold still on any tender area for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily, and allow the tissue to release. | Slowly shift your hips in small circles or side-to-side movements to explore and address surrounding tissue. | Continue for 30 to 90 seconds total, then carefully remove the ball and repeat on the opposite side.
tRu: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. Place the rollball beneath your right glute, roughly in the center of the hip area where the piriformis sits. | Перекрестите правую лодыжку над левым коленом так, чтобы правая нога сформировала цифру 4. tHe: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat. t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you. nE: Roll Ball Posterior Tibialis (Single Leg) Side Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка задней большеберцовой на одной ноге лёжа на боку на полу

t: Place a rollball on the floor and sit on your side, preparing to lower the inner surface of your lower leg onto the ball. | Lie on your side with your bottom arm extended or bent for head support, keeping your body in a comfortable straight line. | Position the rollball under the inner aspect of the lower leg of your bottom leg — roughly between the back of the shin bone (tibia) and the calf, where the posterior tibialis runs. | Stack your top leg either directly on top of the bottom leg or rest it slightly in front on the floor for additional stability. | Allow the weight of your lower leg to sink into the ball; do not press down forcefully with your hands or the top leg. | Slowly roll the leg forward and backward along the inner lower leg, scanning from just above the ankle to below the knee to locate tender spots. | When you find an area of increased sensitivity, pause and hold steady for 20–45 seconds, breathing slowly until you feel the tension begin to soften. | Continue rolling to any additional tight areas, spending equal time on each. | To finish, use your hands to lift the leg off the ball, set the ball aside, and rest for a moment before switching sides or standing up.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and lie face down with the ball positioned just inside your hip bone, in the lower-abdominal region where the psoas runs. | Support your upper body on your forearms, keeping your spine in a neutral position. | Shift your body weight gradually onto the ball until you feel moderate pressure on the target area. Avoid pressing into bone. | Hold the initial position and take two to three slow, deep breaths to allow the tissue to relax. | Make small, slow movements — shifting slightly side to side or up and down — to find areas of greater tension. | When you locate a tender spot, hold still on that point for 20 to 30 seconds or until you feel the tissue soften. | Reduce pressure by shifting weight back onto your forearms before moving the ball to an adjacent area. | Work along the psoas path in the abdominal region for a total of 60 to 90 seconds per side. | To finish, press up onto your forearms, remove the ball, and rest briefly before rolling the opposite side.

t: Lie face down on a firm surface such as a mat or carpet. Place the rollball on the floor beneath your abdomen, positioning it just below your navel and to one side of the midline. | Lower your body slowly onto the ball, supporting your upper body on your forearms to control how much of your weight presses into the abdominal tissue. | Begin with light pressure — only a fraction of your bodyweight — and assess your sensitivity before adding more load. | Slowly roll the ball in small, deliberate strokes along the length of the rectus abdominis, moving from just below the navel upward toward the lower ribs. | When you find a tender or tight spot, stop rolling and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds. Breathe slowly through the hold and allow the tissue to relax under the compression. | After each hold, continue rolling — either continuing upward toward the ribs or shifting slightly toward the midline — to cover the full surface of the rectus abdominis on that side. | Adjust the amount of pressure by shifting more or less body weight through your forearms. Never press down sharply or bounce into the tissue. | Spend 60–90 seconds working one side, then reposition the ball to the opposite side of the midline and repeat. | Finish by rolling gently off the ball, pressing into a hands-and-knees position, and taking two or three slow, full breaths to let the abdomen fully release.

t: Place the rollball on the floor and position yourself face down (prone) with the ball under the front of one thigh, roughly in the center of the quadriceps just below the hip crease. | Support your upper body with your forearms flat on the floor, elbows directly beneath your shoulders, keeping your spine neutral. | Extend the working leg straight so the front of the thigh rests on the rollball. t: Lie on your back on a firm surface with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. | Place the massage ball beneath your upper back, positioning it between your spine and one shoulder blade to target the rhomboid area — not directly on the spine. | Cross both arms over your chest, or reach one arm across your body, to retract the shoulder blade and expose the rhomboid muscle beneath it. | Press through your feet to lift your hips slightly, loading your body weight onto the ball. | Slowly shift your body up and down, or side to side, rolling the ball across the rhomboid area in small, controlled movements. | When you find a tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure there for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the tissue to soften. | Continue rolling across the full rhomboid region — from the upper border near the base of your neck down to the lower border near the mid-back — for 60–90 seconds per side. | Lower your hips, reposition the ball to the opposite side of your spine, and repeat on the other shoulder.

t: Stand with your back facing a wall and place the rollball between the wall and the upper back, just beside the base of your neck at the top of the shoulder blade. | Lean your body weight into the wall to compress the ball against the target area — the levator scapulae attachment near the superior angle of the scapula. | Adjust your feet a few inches away from the wall so you can control the amount of pressure applied through your bodyweight. | Tilt and rotate your head gently away from the side being worked to lengthen the levator scapulae and increase the stretch on the tissue. | Hold still on any tender point for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing slowly and allowing the muscle to relax into the pressure. | Make small, controlled movements — shifting slightly up, down, or sideways — to locate additional areas of tension along the muscle. | Reduce pressure by standing more upright if the sensation becomes too intense; increase pressure by leaning further into the wall. | Once the area feels released, move the ball to an adjacent tender spot and repeat the process. | Complete the work on one side before repositioning the ball to mirror the same area on the opposite side.

t: Sit or stand beside a wall and hold the rollball in the hand on the side you intend to work. | Place the rollball between the wall and the upper back, positioning it just above the top inner corner of the shoulder blade where the levator scapulae attaches. | Lean gently into the wall so the ball takes on a comfortable amount of your body weight — you should feel noticeable pressure without sharp pain. | Drop that shoulder slightly downward to lengthen the levator scapulae and allow the ball to sink into the muscle. | Slowly rotate your head away from the side being worked and tuck your chin slightly toward the opposite collar bone to deepen the stretch. | Hold this position and breathe deeply, allowing the muscle to relax and soften into the ball for 20–40 seconds. | To explore the tissue further, make small, slow head rotations or gently nod your chin up and down while maintaining contact with the ball. | Release the pressure gradually, reposition the ball slightly higher or lower if needed, and repeat on the same spot or move to an adjacent area. | Switch sides and repeat the full sequence on the opposite levator scapulae.

t: Sit on the floor with both legs extended loosely in front of you, or bend one knee slightly outward to open the inner thigh of the leg you will work on. | Place the rollball on the floor against your inner thigh, positioning it high near the groin crease where the pectineus runs between the pubic bone and the upper femur. | Shift your body weight gently toward that side so the rollball makes firm contact with the pectineus — use your hands on the floor behind you for support and balance. | Allow the weight of your thigh to sink into the ball rather than forcing pressure downward; the target sensation is a tolerable, deep ache rather than sharp pain. | Breathe slowly and hold the initial position for 20–30 seconds to let the surrounding tissue begin to relax. | Make small, deliberate movements — gently rolling the ball a centimeter or two in any direction — to scan for areas of increased tenderness within the pectineus. | When you find a sensitive spot, stop moving and hold sustained pressure there, breathing deeply until you feel the tension soften — typically 20–45 seconds per point. | Reposition the ball to cover any remaining tight areas along the upper inner thigh, repeating the hold-and-breathe approach at each location. | To finish, shift your weight off the ball, remove it from beneath your thigh, and gently bring the leg back to a neutral position before switching sides if needed.

nE: Roll Ball Side Lying Scalene Muscles Activation
nR: Активация лестничных лёжа на боку мячом
nH: הפעלת סקלנים בשכיבה צדדית עם כדור
t: Place a rollball on an exercise mat and lie on your side, keeping your body in a straight line from head to hips. | Stack your knees and bend them slightly for stability; rest your bottom arm extended along the floor or use it to lightly support your head. | Lift your head and slide the rollball beneath the lateral side of your neck, positioning it roughly midway between your ear and the top of your shoulder. | Lower your head gently onto the ball so its weight alone provides the pressure — do not push down actively. | Breathe slowly and allow the scalene muscles to soften under the sustained contact for 20–30 seconds. | Make small adjustments — tilt your chin slightly toward the ceiling or let it drop toward your chest — to shift pressure across the anterior, middle, and posterior scalene fibers. | When you find a tender spot, hold steady and breathe through the discomfort until it softens, typically 20–45 seconds. | Reposition the ball slightly higher or lower along the lateral neck to address additional areas of tightness. | To finish, support your head with your top hand, lift it clear of the ball, then roll onto your back and rest for a moment before repeating on the opposite side.

nE: Roll Ball Side Lying Scalene Muscles Activation (side POV)
nR: Активация лестничных лёжа на боку мячом (вид сбоку)
nH: הפעלת סקלנים בשכיבה צדדית עם כדור (מבט צד)
t: Place the rollball on the floor or a firm, non-slip surface. Lie on your side and position the rollball under the lateral side of your neck, roughly between your ear and the top of your shoulder. | Allow your head to rest gently onto the rollball, using only the natural weight of your head to create pressure. Rest your top arm along your hip or on the floor in front of you for stability. | Take a slow breath in and exhale fully, letting your neck muscles relax around the ball. Avoid pressing your head down with any additional force. | Begin a slow scan by making very small movements with your head — shifting slightly forward toward your collarbone, then slightly back toward your spine — to work across the scalene muscle group. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause and hold still. Breathe slowly and steadily for 20–30 seconds, allowing the pressure to gradually release the tissue. | Adjust the height of the ball contact by gently tucking or extending your chin slightly to access different portions of the scalene muscles along the lateral neck. | Continue scanning the lateral neck for 60–90 seconds total. If you feel any pain, tingling, or numbness at any point, lift your head immediately and remove the ball. | Carefully lift your head, remove the rollball, and rest for a moment before repeating on the opposite side if needed.

Задняя большеберцовая мышца лежит глубоко под икрой, поэтому расположите мяч ближе к кости, чем к задней поверхности икры. | Мягко положите голову на массажный мяч, используя только естественный вес головы для давления. Если вы почувствуете боль, покалывание или онемение в какой-либо момент, немедленно поднимите голову и уберите мяч. | Осторожно поднимите голову, снимите ролик и отдохните немного перед повторением с противоположной стороны, если необходимо.

nH: שחרור מותח הירך הצדדי עם כדור
t: Place the rollball on the floor and sit or lie on your side so that the outer hip area — just below and slightly forward of the hip bone — rests on the ball. | Support your upper body with your forearm and opposite hand on the floor to control how much bodyweight you sink onto the ball. | Shift your weight gradually until you feel the rollball make contact with the TFL. The target area is the outer front of the hip, just below the iliac crest. | Breathe slowly and allow your body to relax into the pressure. Avoid tensing the hip — let gravity do the work. | Once you find a tender spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that point for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tissue begin to release. | Slowly roll the ball in small, controlled circles or inch it slightly forward and backward along the TFL to cover the full muscle belly. | If you hit a particularly tight or sensitive area, pause again and sustain pressure until the tension softens. | Gently roll off the ball, rest for a moment, then repeat on the same side or switch to the other hip. | Perform 1–2 minutes of rolling per side, moving slowly and deliberately throughout.

t: Place a rollball on the floor and kneel or sit on the ground with one leg extended or bent in front of you. | Position the rollball under the front of your lower leg, just below the knee, against the tibialis anterior muscle on the outer edge of the shin bone. | Support your upper body with your hands on the floor behind you or to the sides to control how much bodyweight you apply. | Press your shin gently down onto the rollball so you feel moderate pressure on the tibialis anterior — not sharp pain. | Slowly roll the ball down toward your ankle in small, deliberate movements, pausing on any tender or tight spots for 5–10 seconds. | Continue rolling from just below the knee to just above the ankle, covering the full length of the muscle belly. | When you find a particularly tight spot, flex and point your foot slowly to encourage the tissue to release. | After completing one pass, roll back up to the starting position and repeat for the desired duration, then switch legs.

t: Sit or stand next to a wall and place the roll ball between the wall and the lower portion of your trapezius, roughly between your shoulder blade and your spine at mid-back height. | Lean your body weight gently into the ball so it presses against the lower trap tissue. t: Lie on your back on a firm surface and place the rollball beneath your mid-to-lower back, positioning it just medial to the inner border of one shoulder blade — this is where the lower trapezius fibers converge toward the thoracic spine. | Bend both knees and plant your feet flat on the floor to give yourself control over how much bodyweight presses into the ball. | Cross your arms over your chest or reach the same-side arm across your body to protract the shoulder blade and expose the lower trapezius fibers beneath it. | Slowly lower your body weight onto the ball, allowing it to sink into the tissue. t: Sit upright on a chair or bench, or stand with your back against a wall for support. Hold the rollball in the hand opposite to the side you plan to work first. | Reach across your body and place the rollball on the upper trapezius of the opposite shoulder — the fleshy ridge of muscle that runs from the base of your neck out toward the top of your shoulder blade. | Apply gentle downward pressure onto the ball using the heel of your hand or your fingertips, pressing the muscle against the ball rather than gripping it. Breathe slowly and allow the muscle to soften under the sustained compression. | While holding on a tender area, gently tilt your head away from the ball — ear toward the opposite shoulder — to dynamically lengthen the upper trapezius and deepen the stretch. | Continue rolling outward in small increments, spending extra time on any areas that feel particularly tight or ropy. | Maintain pressure at a tolerable 4–6 on a 10-point discomfort scale throughout. Adjust by pressing the ball more or less firmly with your hand. | Work through one side for 60–90 seconds, then switch the ball to the other hand and repeat on the opposite shoulder.

t: Place the rollball on a firm surface or hold it in your hand, and position yourself so you can press the ball against your upper trapezius — the area between the top of your shoulder and the base of your neck. | You can perform this seated, standing against a wall, or lying on your side, whichever allows you to control the pressure comfortably. | Slowly roll the ball along the upper trapezius from the base of your neck toward the top of your shoulder, pausing whenever you find a tender spot. | When you locate a tight area, hold the ball still on that point and maintain moderate pressure for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily. | Relax the muscle as much as possible while the ball holds pressure — avoid tensing the shoulder upward. | After the hold, gently tilt your head away from the side being worked to increase the stretch through the upper trapezius. | Continue rolling slowly along the muscle, repeating the pause-and-hold at each tender point. | Work the full length of the upper trapezius, then switch sides and repeat the process.

t: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie face-down with your body fully extended. | Position the roller under one upper arm, just below the shoulder, with your palm facing the floor. | Extend the working arm out to the side at roughly a 45–90° angle from your torso so the biceps rests directly on top of the roller. | Support your body weight on your opposite forearm and the toes of both feet. | Slowly roll the foam roller down your upper arm from just below the shoulder toward the crease of the elbow, using gentle pressure. | Pause for 2–3 seconds on any tight or tender spot, maintaining steady pressure without forcing through sharp pain. | Continue rolling back up toward the shoulder, working the full length of the biceps brachii. | Complete 30–60 seconds on one arm, then switch to the other side.

t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place a foam roller under both calves, just above the Achilles tendon. | Put your hands on the floor behind your hips and press down to lift your glutes off the ground, transferring your body weight onto the roller. | Cross one ankle over the other to stack weight on a single calf and increase pressure. | Slowly roll toward your knee until the roller reaches just below the back of the knee, then reverse the motion back toward the ankle. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for 20–30 seconds and let the tissue relax before continuing. | After completing one leg, switch by uncrossing your ankles, cross the opposite ankle on top, and repeat on the other calf. | Work each calf for 60–90 seconds, targeting both the center of the muscle (gastrocnemius) and the sides to reach the soleus underneath. | Finish by gently flexing and pointing your foot a few times to encourage blood flow through the released tissue.
tRu: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place a foam roller under both calves, just above the Achilles tendon. | Put your hands on the floor behind your hips and press down to lift your glutes off the ground, transferring your body weight onto the roller. | Перекрестите одну лодыжку над другой, чтобы перенести вес на одно икроножное мышцу и увеличить давление. | Slowly roll toward your knee until the roller reaches just below the back of the knee, then reverse the motion back toward the ankle. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for 20–30 seconds and let the tissue relax before continuing. | Выполнив одну ногу, переключитесь, расскрестив лодыжки, скрестив противоположную лодыжку сверху, и повторите на другую икру. | Work each calf for 60–90 seconds, targeting both the center of the muscle (gastrocnemius) and the sides to reach the soleus underneath. | Завершите, плавно сгибая и разгибая стопу несколько раз, чтобы стимулировать кровоток в расслабленных тканях.
tHe: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place a foam roller under both calves, just above the Achilles tendon. | Put your hands on the floor behind your hips and press down to lift your glutes off the ground, transferring your body weight onto the roller. | חצה את קרסול אחד מעל השנייה כדי להניח משקל על שריר השוק בודד ולהגביר את הלחץ. | Slowly roll toward your knee until the roller reaches just below the back of the knee, then reverse the motion back toward the ankle. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for 20–30 seconds and let the tissue relax before continuing. | אחרי שסיימת רגל אחת, החלף על ידי שחרור הצלבת הקרסוליים, הצלב את הקרסול הנגדי מעל, וחזור על התרגיל בשוק השנייה. | Work each calf for 60–90 seconds, targeting both the center of the muscle (gastrocnemius) and the sides to reach the soleus underneath. | סיים בכיפוף ופשיטה עדינים של כף הרגל מספר פעמים כדי לעודד זרימת דם ברקמה המשוחררת.

nH: גלגול תאומים ברגל אחת עם רולר
t: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the foam roller under your right calf, just above the Achilles tendon. | Cross your left ankle over your right shin to stack your body weight onto the right leg. | Place your hands flat on the floor behind your hips and press down to lift your glutes off the ground. | Slowly roll forward along the calf until the roller reaches just below the back of your knee, then reverse the direction. | Move at a steady, controlled pace — roughly one to two seconds in each direction — rather than rolling quickly. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for two to three seconds and let the pressure release before continuing. | After completing the full length of the calf, rotate your leg slightly inward and then outward to expose the inner and outer portions of the gastrocnemius and soleus. | Finish the set, then switch legs by placing the roller under your left calf and crossing your right ankle over for the same sequence.
tRu: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the foam roller under your right calf, just above the Achilles tendon. | Перекрестите левую лодыжку над правой голенью, чтобы перенести вес тела на правую ногу. | Положите ладони плашмя на пол за бёдрами и нажмите вниз, чтобы приподнять ягодицы над полом. | Slowly roll forward along the calf until the roller reaches just below the back of your knee, then reverse the direction. | Двигайтесь в устойчивом, контролируемом темпе — примерно одна-две секунды в каждом направлении — вместо того, чтобы перекатываться быстро. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for two to three seconds and let the pressure release before continuing. | Пройдя всю длину икры, слегка разверните ногу внутрь, а затем наружу, чтобы проработать внутреннюю и внешнюю части икроножной и камбаловидной мышц. | Завершите подход, затем поменяйте ноги, положив роллер под левое икроножное muscle и перекрестив правую голень над левой для выполнения той же последовательности.
tHe: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you and place the foam roller under your right calf, just above the Achilles tendon. | חצה את קרסול שמאל מעל שוק ימין כדי לעמוס את משקל הגוף על הרגל הימנית. | Place your hands flat on the floor behind your hips and press down to lift your glutes off the ground. | Slowly roll forward along the calf until the roller reaches just below the back of your knee, then reverse the direction. | Move at a steady, controlled pace — roughly one to two seconds in each direction — rather than rolling quickly. | When you find a tender or tight spot, pause on it for two to three seconds and let the pressure release before continuing. | אחרי שסיימת את כל אורך השוק, סובב את הרגל מעט פנימה ואז החוצה כדי לחשוף את החלקים הפנימי והחיצוני של התאומים והסוליה. | סיים את הסט, ואז החלף רגליים: הנח את הרולר מתחת לשוק שמאל והצלב את קרסול ימין מעליו לאותה רצף.

nH: גלגול חזה בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Place a foam roller on the floor horizontally. | Lie face down and position the roller under your chest, just below your collarbone, with your arms extended forward or out to the sides for support. | Support most of your weight on your forearms or hands and lightly brace your core so your lower back does not sag. | Slowly shift your body forward so the roller moves down toward the middle of your chest, then shift back to move it toward the upper chest. | When you reach a tender spot, pause for 20–30 seconds and breathe deeply to let the tissue relax before continuing. | Continue rolling at a slow, even pace across the full width of your chest, spending extra time on tight areas. | To target one side more specifically, tilt your body slightly to that side and shift your weight onto the corresponding pectoral. | After 30–60 seconds of rolling, or once the tissue feels less restricted, gently press up with your arms and lift yourself off the roller.

nE: Roll Chest Opener Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка груди с раскрытием лёжа на полу
nH: גלגול פתיחת חזה בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Place a foam roller on the floor and sit at one end of it with your knees bent and feet flat. | Slowly lower yourself backward so the roller runs lengthwise along your entire spine, from tailbone to the base of your skull. | Keep your knees bent and feet flat on the floor to stabilise your lower body throughout the stretch. | Let your arms fall out to the sides with palms facing up, positioning them between 45° and 90° relative to your torso — find the angle where you feel the most tension across your chest. | Allow gravity to draw your chest open and your shoulders toward the floor, breathing steadily and without forcing the stretch. | Hold the position for 30–60 seconds, taking slow, deep breaths to encourage progressive relaxation of the chest and anterior shoulders. | To finish, bring your arms back to your sides, roll to one side, and use your hands to press yourself back up to seated.
tRu: Положите валик для пены на пол и сядьте на одном его конце, согнув колени и поставив ступни на пол. | Slowly lower yourself backward so the roller runs lengthwise along your entire spine, from tailbone to the base of your skull. | Держите колени согнутыми и ступни прижатыми к полу для стабилизации нижней части тела на протяжении растяжки. | Дайте вашим рукам висеть вдоль тела с ладонями вверх, располагая их под углом 45° и 90° относительно корпуса — найдите угол, в котором вы чувствуете наибольшее напряжение в груди. | Позвольте гравитации раскрыть грудь и опустить плечи к полу, дышите ровно и не форсируйте растяжку. | Держите положение в течение 30-60 секунд, делая медленные, глубокие вдохи для поощрения постепенного расслабления груди и передних дельт. | To finish, bring your arms back to your sides, roll to one side, and use your hands to press yourself back up to seated.

nE: Roll Erector Spinae Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка разгибателей спины лёжа на полу
nH: גלגול זוקפי הגב בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Place a foam roller horizontally on the floor. Sit on the floor in front of it with your knees bent and feet flat. | Lean back and position the foam roller just below your shoulder blades, supporting your upper body with your hands behind your head or crossed over your chest. | Lift your hips off the floor so your body weight shifts onto the roller and your feet. | Using your feet to control movement, slowly roll the foam roller down toward your lower back, targeting the erector spinae on either side of the spine. | Pause on any tender or tight spot for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply to allow the tissue to release. | Continue rolling slowly down until the roller reaches the top of your hips, stopping before it reaches the tailbone. | Roll back up toward the shoulder blades at the same controlled pace, working the full length of the paraspinal muscles. | Repeat the pass 2–3 times, spending extra time on areas that feel particularly tight. | To finish, lower your hips to the floor, remove the roller, and rest for a moment with your knees pulled gently to your chest.

Сядьте на пол перед ним, согнув колени и поставив ступни на пол. | Отклонитесь назад и расположите foam roller чуть ниже лопаток, поддерживая верхнюю часть тела руками за головой или скрестив на груди. | Поднимите таз с пола, чтобы вес тела сместился на ролик и на ваши ноги. | Using your feet to control movement, slowly roll the foam roller down toward your lower back, targeting the erector spinae on either side of the spine. | Пауза на любой болезненной или напряжённой точке на 20–30 секунд, дышите глубоко, чтобы позволить тканям расслабиться. | Продолжайте медленно кататься вниз, пока валик не достигнет верха ваших бёдер, остановившись перед тем, как он дойдёт до копчика. | Roll back up toward the shoulder blades at the same controlled pace, working the full length of the paraspinal muscles. | Repeat the pass 2–3 times, spending extra time on areas that feel particularly tight. | To finish, lower your hips to the floor, remove the roller, and rest for a moment with your knees pulled gently to your chest.

t: Place a foam roller or massage ball on the floor in front of a wall or sturdy surface you can hold for balance. | Stand or sit in a chair and position the roller under the arch of one bare foot. | Apply moderate downward pressure by shifting your body weight onto that foot — use the wall or chair for balance if standing. | Slowly roll the foot forward so the roller moves toward the ball of the foot, then roll back toward the heel. | Maintain a slow, controlled pace — roughly one full pass every two to three seconds. | When you reach a tender spot, pause for five to ten seconds and breathe steadily before continuing. | Continue rolling the full length of the sole for thirty to sixty seconds. | Shift the foot slightly inward or outward to cover the medial arch and lateral edge of the foot. | Switch feet and repeat the same sequence on the other side.
tRu: Положите валик для пены, сложенное полотенце или твердую подушку на пол перед стеной или прочной поверхностью, за которую можно держаться для равновесия. | Stand or sit in a chair and position the roller under the arch of one bare foot. | Умеренно надавите вниз, перенеся вес тела на эту стопу — при стойке используйте стену или стул для равновесия. | Slowly roll the foot forward so the roller moves toward the ball of the foot, then roll back toward the heel. | Сохраняйте медленный, контролируемый темп — примерно одно полное движение каждые два-три секунды. | When you reach a tender spot, pause for five to ten seconds and breathe steadily before continuing. | Продолжайте катать всю длисть стопы в течение тридцати-шестидесяти секунд. | Shift the foot slightly inward or outward to cover the medial arch and lateral edge of the foot. | Switch feet and repeat the same sequence on the other side.

nH: גלגול אמות בעמידה על הקיר עם רולר
t: Stand facing a wall and hold a foam roller horizontally against it at roughly waist to chest height. | Place both forearms on top of the roller so the roller sits between your forearms and the wall, with your palms facing down or inward. | Lean your body weight gently into the wall to press your forearms onto the roller and create the desired amount of compression. | Slowly roll your forearms upward a few centimeters, then back downward, covering the length from just below the wrist to just below the elbow. | When you find a tender spot, pause and hold the pressure there for 20 to 30 seconds while keeping your breath steady. | Continue rolling in short strokes, spending extra time on areas of notable tightness. | After covering the back of the forearms, rotate your arms so the palms face up and repeat the rolling motion on the flexor side. | Step back from the wall, lower your arms, and shake them out gently to finish.
tRu: Stand facing a wall and hold a foam roller horizontally against it at roughly waist to chest height. | Поставьте обе предплечья на верхнюю часть валика так, чтобы валик находился между вашими предплечьями и стеной, с ладонями, направленными вниз или внутрь. | Плавно перенесите вес тела на стену, чтобы предплечья давили на валик и создавали желаемое количество сжатия. | Slowly roll your forearms upward a few centimeters, then back downward, covering the length from just below the wrist to just below the elbow. | When you find a tender spot, pause and hold the pressure there for 20 to 30 seconds while keeping your breath steady. | Продолжайте кататься короткими движениями, уделяя больше времени участкам с заметным напряжением. | Пройдя заднюю поверхность предплечий, разверните руки ладонями вверх и повторите прокатывающее движение на стороне сгибателей. | Step back from the wall, lower your arms, and shake them out gently to finish.

nE: Roll Front Shoulder and Chest Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка передней дельты и груди лёжа на полу
nH: גלגול קדמת כתף וחזה בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר

nE: Roll Posterior Shoulder Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка задней дельты лёжа на полу

t: Place the foam roller horizontally on the floor. Lie on your back and shift to one side so the roller sits beneath the back of your target shoulder, roughly at the rear deltoid where the shoulder meets the upper back. | Extend the arm on the target side straight out to the side at shoulder height, palm facing up, to open the posterior shoulder and allow full contact with the foam. | Bend both knees and plant your feet flat on the floor to stabilize your lower body and prevent rolling away from the target area. | Allow your full bodyweight to settle onto the roller. nE: Roll Quadriceps (Vastus Lateralis) Lying on Floor

t: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie face down (prone) with the roller positioned horizontally under your right thigh, just below the hip crease. | Angle your body slightly so the roller contacts the outer portion of the thigh — the vastus lateralis — rather than the center of the quad. | Prop yourself up on your forearms, keeping your elbows directly beneath your shoulders to support your upper body. | Keep your left leg resting on the floor or bend it to the side to reduce bodyweight on the roller; straighten it and stack both thighs to increase pressure. | Press your forearms into the floor and slowly pull your body forward so the roller travels down the outer thigh toward the knee. | Move at a slow, controlled pace — roughly one inch per second — and pause for five to ten seconds on any tender or tight spot. | Reverse the movement, pushing yourself back so the roller travels up the outer thigh toward the hip. | Continue rolling the full length of the vastus lateralis for thirty to sixty seconds, then reposition and repeat on the left leg.

nH: מתיחת מסובבי ירך ופושטי ירך בשכיבה עם רולר (רגליים מוצלבות)
t: Place a foam roller on the floor. Lower your hips so your weight rests on the roller. | Use your hands and left foot on the floor to shift your bodyweight slightly to the right — toward the side of the crossed leg — so the roller applies focused compression to the right gluteus maximus and external rotators. | Breathe in slowly, then exhale fully and let the target muscles relax into the roller. Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, continuing to breathe steadily. | Nudge your hips gently forward or backward to explore different contact points along the glute and upper hamstring. Pause on any area that feels tight or tender for an additional 20–30 seconds. | When finished, plant your left foot firmly, shift your hips off the roller, uncross your right leg, and lower both feet to the floor. | Switch sides: cross your left ankle over your right thigh and reposition the roller under the right glute to repeat on the opposite side.

t: Kneel on a mat and place the foam roller on the floor perpendicular to your body, in front of your shins. | Lower the front of one shin onto the roller, positioning it just below the knee cap. | Support your upper body through your hands on the floor and the opposite knee, controlling how much weight you place on the roller. | Slowly roll down toward the ankle, covering the full length of the tibialis anterior from just below the knee to just above the ankle. | Pause for 2–3 seconds on any spot that feels particularly tight or tender before continuing. | Rotate your leg slightly inward and outward to address the full width of the muscle belly, not just the center. | Complete the full sequence, then switch legs and repeat.
tRu: Встаньте на колени на коврике и положите foam roller на пол перпендикулярно телу, перед голенями. | Плавно опустите переднюю часть голени на ролик, разместив его чуть ниже коленной чашечки. | Support your upper body through your hands on the floor and the opposite knee, controlling how much weight you place on the roller. | Slowly roll down toward the ankle, covering the full length of the tibialis anterior from just below the knee to just above the ankle. | Задержитесь на 2–3 секунды в любой точке, которая ощущается особенно напряжённой или болезненной, прежде чем продолжить. | Rotate your leg slightly inward and outward to address the full width of the muscle belly, not just the center. | Выполните полную последовательность, затем поменяйте ноги и повторите.

nE: Roll Tibialis Anterior (Single Leg) Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка передней большеберцовой на одной ноге лёжа на полу
nH: גלגול טיביאליס קדמי ברגל אחת בשכיבה על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Lie face down on the floor and place the foam roller perpendicular to your lower leg, positioning it just below the knee on the upper shin. | Extend the working leg fully and rest the opposite leg on the floor beside it, or cross it over the working leg to add more pressure. | Prop yourself up on your forearms, keeping your core lightly engaged and your upper body relaxed. | Shift enough body weight onto the roller so you feel moderate pressure along the tibialis anterior — the muscle running beside the shinbone. | Slowly roll down the shin toward the ankle in a controlled 2–3 second stroke, keeping the movement smooth and deliberate. | Roll back up toward the knee with the same slow pace, covering the full length of the muscle belly. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that area for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | Continue rolling up and down for 30–60 seconds total on the working leg. | Lower that leg to the floor, switch sides, and repeat the full sequence on the other leg.
tRu: Лягте на живот на полу и положите валик для пены перпендикулярно нижней ноге, расположив его чуть ниже колена на верхней части голени. | Полностью выпрямите рабочую ногу и положите рядом на пол противоположную ногу, либо перекрестите её над рабочей ногой для большего давления. | Prop yourself up on your forearms, keeping your core lightly engaged and your upper body relaxed. | Shift enough body weight onto the roller so you feel moderate pressure along the tibialis anterior — the muscle running beside the shinbone. | Slowly roll down the shin toward the ankle in a controlled 2–3 second stroke, keeping the movement smooth and deliberate. | Roll back up toward the knee with the same slow pace, covering the full length of the muscle belly. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that area for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | Продолжайте перекатываться вверх и вниз в течение 30–60 секунд на рабочей ноге. | Опустите эту ногу на пол, поменяйте стороны и повторите всю последовательность на другой ноге.
tHe: Lie face down on the floor and place the foam roller perpendicular to your lower leg, positioning it just below the knee on the upper shin. | פשוט את הרגל הפעילה לגמרי והנח את הרגל הנגדית על הרצפה לצידה, או חצה אותה מעל הרגל הפעילה כדי להוסיף לחץ. | Prop yourself up on your forearms, keeping your core lightly engaged and your upper body relaxed. | Shift enough body weight onto the roller so you feel moderate pressure along the tibialis anterior — the muscle running beside the shinbone. | Slowly roll down the shin toward the ankle in a controlled 2–3 second stroke, keeping the movement smooth and deliberate. | Roll back up toward the knee with the same slow pace, covering the full length of the muscle belly. | When you reach a tender or tight spot, pause and hold steady pressure on that area for 20–30 seconds until you feel the tension release. | המשיך להתגלגל למעלה ולמטה בסך הכל 30–60 שניות על הרגל הפעילה. | Lower that leg to the floor, switch sides, and repeat the full sequence on the other leg.

nE: Roll Triceps Side Lying on Floor
nR: Прокатка трицепса лёжа на боку на полу
nH: גלגול יד אחורית בשכיבה צדדית על הרצפה עם רולר
t: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie on your side with the arm you want to work extended along the floor above your head. | Position the back of your upper arm (triceps area) on top of the roller, just above the elbow. | Stack your hips and keep your body in a straight line, using your free hand on the floor in front of you for light support. | Lift your hips slightly off the floor so your body weight creates pressure through the upper arm onto the roller. | Slowly roll from just above the elbow toward the back of the shoulder, pausing anywhere you feel tightness or discomfort. | Hold on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds, allowing the tissue to soften before moving on. | Continue rolling the full length of the triceps area for 60 to 90 seconds, then switch sides.
tRu: Положите валик для пены на пол и лягте на бок с вытянутой вдоль пола над головой рукой, которую вы хотите проработать. | Position the back of your upper arm (triceps area) on top of the roller, just above the elbow. | Stack your hips and keep your body in a straight line, using your free hand on the floor in front of you for light support. | Поднимите таз немного с пола, чтобы вес тела создавал давление через верхнюю руку на ролик. | Slowly roll from just above the elbow toward the back of the shoulder, pausing anywhere you feel tightness or discomfort. | Удерживайте на болезненных точках 20–30 секунд, позволяя тканям расслабиться перед переходом. | Продолжайте катать всю длисть трицепса в течение 60–90 секунд, затем поменяйте стороны.
tHe: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie on your side with the arm you want to work extended along the floor above your head. | Position the back of your upper arm (triceps area) on top of the roller, just above the elbow. | Stack your hips and keep your body in a straight line, using your free hand on the floor in front of you for light support. | Lift your hips slightly off the floor so your body weight creates pressure through the upper arm onto the roller. | Slowly roll from just above the elbow toward the back of the shoulder, pausing anywhere you feel tightness or discomfort. | Hold on tender spots for 20 to 30 seconds, allowing the tissue to soften before moving on. | המשילו להתגלגל את כל אורך שריר הירך הצידי למשך שלושים עשרים עד שישים שניות, ואז הזיזו מחדש את הגלגל וחזרו על התרגיל ברגל השמאלית.

t: Sit on the floor with the foam roller placed horizontally on the mat directly behind you. | Lower your mid-back onto the roller, plant both feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and bend your knees to roughly 90°. | Cross your arms over your chest or interlace your hands behind your head to draw the shoulder blades apart and expose the upper back muscles. | Press through your feet to lift your hips slightly off the floor, shifting your body weight between your feet and the roller. | Slowly roll the foam roller upward along your thoracic spine toward your upper back, using your feet to control the movement. | Pause for 2–3 seconds on any spot that feels particularly tight or tender, letting your body weight sink into the roller. | Continue rolling in small increments until the roller sits between your shoulder blades and upper trapezius region. | Reverse direction and slowly roll back down to the starting position, then repeat for the desired number of passes or duration.
tRu: Sit on the floor with the foam roller placed horizontally on the mat directly behind you. | Опустите среднюю часть спины на ролик, поставьте обе ноги на пол на ширине тазобедренных суставов и согните колени примерно под углом 90°. | Перекрестите руки на груди или переплетите пальцы за головой, чтобы развести лопатки и подчеркнуть мышцы верхней спины. | Press through your feet to lift your hips slightly off the floor, shifting your body weight between your feet and the roller. | Slowly roll the foam roller upward along your thoracic spine toward your upper back, using your feet to control the movement. | Задержитесь на 2–3 секунды в любой точке, которая ощущается особенно напряжённой или болезненной, позволяя вашему весу погружаться в валик. | Продолжайте кататься небольшими отрезками, пока валик не окажется между вашими лопатками и верхней частью трапециевидной мышцы. | Reverse direction and slowly roll back down to the starting position, then repeat for the desired number of passes or duration.
tHe: Sit on the floor with the foam roller placed horizontally on the mat directly behind you. | Lower your mid-back onto the roller, plant both feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, and bend your knees to roughly 90°. | חצה את ידיך מעל החזה שלך או ערבב את הידיים מאחורי הראש כדי למשוך את כתפיים ולחשוף את שרירי הגב העליונים. | Press through your feet to lift your hips slightly off the floor, shifting your body weight between your feet and the roller. | Slowly roll the foam roller upward along your thoracic spine toward your upper back, using your feet to control the movement. | Pause for 2–3 seconds on any spot that feels particularly tight or tender, letting your body weight sink into the roller. | המשילו להתגלגל עד שגופכם כמעט מקביל לרצפה או עד שאתם מגיעים לטווח המרבי שאתם יכולים לשלוט בו בלי שהירכיים שלכם יירדו או הגב שלכם יתמוטט. | Reverse direction and slowly roll back down to the starting position, then repeat for the desired number of passes or duration.

t: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and feet together. Reach both arms straight overhead close to your ears, pressing your lower back gently into the floor. | Inhale to prepare, drawing your navel gently toward your spine to engage your core. | Exhale as you float your arms toward the ceiling and begin to curl your head and shoulders off the floor, leading with the crown of your head rather than your chin. | Continue exhaling as you peel your spine off the floor one vertebra at a time, rolling through your mid-back and then lower back in a slow, sequential wave. | Reach your arms forward toward your feet and fold at the hips into a seated forward bend, keeping your spine as long as possible. | Hold the stretched position for one breath, feeling the lengthening through your lower back and waist. | Inhale, then exhale as you begin rolling back down by tilting your pelvis posteriorly and lowering your lumbar spine to the floor vertebra by vertebra. | Continue lowering through your mid-back, upper back, and finally your head, returning your arms overhead to the starting position. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining the same slow, controlled tempo in both directions.
tRu: Лягте на спину с ногами, выпрямленными и ступнями вместе. Вытяните обе руки прямо над головой близко к ушам, слегка прижимая поясницу к полу. | Вдыхайте, чтобы подготовиться, мягко втягивая пупок к позвоночнику, чтобы активировать мышцы кора. | Выдыхайте, когда поднимаете руки к потолку и начинаете поднимать голову и плечи от пола, ведя макушкой, а не подбородком. | Продолжайте выдыхать, когда вы приподнимаете позвоночник с пола позвонок за позвонком, перекатываясь через среднюю спину, а затем через нижнюю в медленной, последовательной волне. | Reach your arms forward toward your feet and fold at the hips into a seated forward bend, keeping your spine as long as possible. | Держите растянутое положение на один вдох, ощущая удлинение по нижней части спины и талии. | Сделайте вдох, затем на выдохе подтяните обе ноги вверх, сгибая колени, двигая ролик к ягодицам. | Продолжайте опускаться через среднюю часть спины, верхнюю часть спины и, наконец, голову, возвращая руки над головой в исходное положение. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining the same slow, controlled tempo in both directions.
tHe: Lie flat on your back with legs extended and feet together. t: Set the Roman chair so the foot rollers sit just above your ankles when you are seated, allowing your legs to be nearly straight or slightly bent. | Sit on the pad and hook your feet under the foot rollers, pressing the tops of your feet firmly against them. | Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands lightly behind your head without interlacing your fingers. | Inhale and slowly lower your torso backward, allowing your lower back to extend past horizontal toward the floor — go only as far as your flexibility and strength allow. | Pause briefly at the bottom without losing tension in your core. | Exhale and contract your rectus abdominis to curl your torso back up toward your thighs. | At the top, squeeze your abs for one count before beginning the next rep. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a controlled tempo on both the lowering and lifting phases.
