nE: Two Legged Inverted Staff Pose Dwi Pada Viparita Dandasana
nR: Перевёрнутый посох на двух ногах (Дви Пада Випарита Дандасана)
nH: תנוחת המטה ההפוך על שתי רגליים דווי פאדה ויפריטה דנדאסאנה
t: Begin lying on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Place your palms on the floor beside your ears, fingers pointing toward your shoulders, and lift into a full wheel (Urdhva Dhanurasana). | Lower the crown of your head to the floor and walk your forearms down one at a time so the elbows are bent and the hands interlace behind the head, forming a triangular base of support. | Press through your forearms and the crown of your head to lift your chest and lengthen your spine upward. | Straighten both legs one at a time, extending them fully along the floor with the feet flat or the toes pressed into the mat. | Draw your shoulder blades together and down your back to broaden the chest and deepen the spinal extension. | Breathe steadily, holding the pose for 5–10 slow breaths while maintaining length through the spine rather than compressing the lower back. | To exit, bend your knees and walk your feet back in, then carefully lower your torso to the floor, returning your head last.
tRu: Лягте на спину, согните колени и поставьте стопы ровно на пол на ширине бёдер. | Положите ладони на пол рядом с ушами, пальцами к плечам, и поднимитесь в полный мост (Урдхва Дханурасана). | Опустите макушку головы на пол и по одной опустите предплечья, чтобы согнуть локти и переплести руки за головой, образуя треугольную опорную базу. | Press through your forearms and the crown of your head to lift your chest and lengthen your spine upward. | Straighten both legs one at a time, extending them fully along the floor with the feet flat or the toes pressed into the mat. | Сожмите лопатки вместе и вниз по спине, чтобы расширить грудь и усилить разгибание в позвоночнике. | Дышите ровно, удерживая позу 5–10 медленных дыханий, сохраняя длину позвоночника, а не прогибая поясницу. | To exit, bend your knees and walk your feet back in, then carefully lower your torso to the floor, returning your head last.

nE: Two Legs Hammer Curl with Towel (VERSION 2)
t: Sit on the floor or on the edge of a firm, flat surface and fold a bath towel lengthwise into a long strip. | Loop the center of the towel around the arches of both feet, then hold one end of the towel in each hand with a neutral grip — palms facing each other as in a hammer curl. | Extend your arms straight and raise both legs off the floor so the towel is taut between your hands and feet before the movement begins. | Sit tall with your spine upright, shoulders pulled back and down, and core braced to prevent your torso from rocking. | Begin the curl by bending both elbows simultaneously, driving your knuckles upward toward your shoulders while keeping your palms facing each other throughout. | Hold your legs steady — your feet and legs are the anchor providing resistance, so any unintended movement of the feet reduces the load. | Continue curling until your hands are at or near shoulder level and you feel a strong contraction in your brachioradialis and upper arms. | Slowly extend your elbows back to the starting position over two to three seconds, maintaining towel tension and keeping your legs elevated. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without allowing the towel to go slack between reps.

nE: Two Legs Reverse Biceps Curl with Towel (VERSION 2)
nR: Обратные сгибания двумя ногами с полотенцем (вариант 2)
nH: כפיפות הפוכות בשתי רגליים עם מגבת (גרסה 2)
t: Loop a towel around a sturdy overhead anchor point — a door frame, pull-up bar, or structural beam — and let both ends hang down within reach. | Lie on your back on the floor directly beneath the anchor, with your arms extended overhead and your hands gripping one end of the towel each, palms facing down (pronated grip). | Raise both legs off the floor and hold them at a comfortable angle, keeping your core braced so your body forms a rigid plank from shoulders to feet. | Exhale and pull your torso upward by driving your elbows toward your hips, keeping the pronated grip throughout the movement. | Continue curling until your hands reach the sides of your chest or your elbows are fully flexed — whichever your range of motion allows. | Hold the top position for a brief pause, squeezing the elbow flexors. | Inhale and lower yourself back to the starting position under full control until your arms are fully extended. | Repeat for the target number of reps without letting your hips sag or your legs drop.

t: Stand with your feet together or hip-width apart and your arms hanging at your sides. | Keep your legs straight or with a very slight bend in the knees to reduce strain on the hamstrings. | Take a breath in, then exhale as you hinge forward at the hips, letting your torso drop toward the floor. | Reach both hands down toward your toes, keeping your neck relaxed so your head hangs naturally. | Go only as far as your flexibility allows without rounding aggressively through the mid-back or losing balance. | Hold the bottom position for two to three seconds, feeling the stretch along your lower back and waist. | Inhale and slowly return to standing by engaging your core and rising through the hips. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions or hold the bottom position as a static stretch.

nR: Прыжки с двух ног на одну
t: Stand with your feet hip-width apart on a firm, flat surface with enough clear space in front of and around you. | Bend your knees and hips into a quarter-squat, swinging your arms back to load the jump. | Drive your arms forward and upward as you extend through your hips, knees, and ankles to jump as high as you comfortably can. | While in the air, identify your landing foot and draw the opposite knee up slightly to prepare for a single-leg landing. | Land softly on the ball of your chosen foot first, then let your heel settle as you absorb the impact by bending your knee and hip — aim for a 45–60° knee bend at the bottom. | Keep your landing knee tracking over your second toe and your torso upright; avoid letting the knee cave inward. | Hold the single-leg landing position for one to two seconds to confirm balance and control before resetting. | Return both feet to the ground, reset your stance, and repeat for the desired number of reps, alternating the landing leg each set or each rep.

t: Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means more horizontal body angle and greater difficulty. | Lie underneath the bar and grip it with a supinated (underhand, palms-up) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. | Extend your legs and drive your heels into the floor so your body forms a straight line from head to heels. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and keep your hips level — your body should remain rigid throughout the movement. | Pull your shoulder blades together and down before initiating the pull. | Drive your elbows toward your hips and pull your chest up to the bar, keeping your elbows close to your torso. | Pause briefly at the top when your chest nearly touches the bar and your shoulder blades are fully retracted. | Lower yourself under control back to the starting position with arms fully extended. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting your hips sag or your core disengage.
tRu: Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means more horizontal body angle and greater difficulty. | Лягте под штангу и возьмите её обратным (нижним, ладонями вверх) хватом, руки на ширине плеч. | Вытяните ноги и упритесь пятками в пол, чтобы тело образовывало прямую линию от головы до пяток. | Напрягите корпус, сожмите ягодицы и держите бёдра на одном уровне — ваше тело должно оставаться напряжённым на протяжении всего движения. | Pull your shoulder blades together and down before initiating the pull. | Двигайте локти к бёдрам и тяните грудь к перекладке, сохраняя локти близко к корпусу. | На мгновение остановитесь в верхней точке, когда ваша грудь почти касается перекладины, а лопатки полностью сведены. | Подконтрольно опуститесь в исходное положение с полностью выпрямленными руками. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting your hips sag or your core disengage.
tHe: Set a bar in a rack or Smith machine at roughly hip height — lower means more horizontal body angle and greater difficulty. | Lie underneath the bar and grip it with a supinated (underhand, palms-up) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. | פתח את הרגליים ודחוץ את עקביך לרצפה כך שגופך יוצר קו ישר מהראש ועד עקבי הרגליים. | תכווץ את שרירי הליבה, כווץ את השרירים הגלוטיאליים, ושמור על ירכיים בגובה אחיד - הגוך צריך להישאר קשיח לאורך כל התנועה. | Pull your shoulder blades together and down before initiating the pull. | הושט את מרפקיך לכיוון המותניים ומשך את החזה שלך לעבר המוט, שמור על מרפקיך קרובים לגופך. | Pause briefly at the top when your chest nearly touches the bar and your shoulder blades are fully retracted. | הורד את עצמך בשליטה חזרה לעמדת המוצא עם ידיים ישרות לגמרי. | Repeat for the desired number of reps without letting your hips sag or your core disengage.

t: Grip a pull-up bar with one hand in a standard overhand position and place your other hand several inches lower — either by gripping a looped towel, a gymnastics ring, or a lower rung — so the two hands are at noticeably different heights. | Hang at full arm extension with both arms, letting your shoulders depress naturally into a passive hang. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes, and cross your ankles to keep your lower body still throughout the set. | Initiate the pull by actively depressing and retracting the shoulder blade on the higher-hand side. | Drive your higher elbow down and back while allowing your lower arm to assist with reduced force. | Pull until your chin clears the bar or until the higher-side elbow reaches full flexion. | Lower yourself under control to full arm extension, maintaining tension rather than dropping passively. | Complete all target reps on one side, then switch hand positions and perform the same number of reps on the opposite side.
tRu: Возьмитесь за перекладину одной рукой в стандартном верхнем положении, а другую руку разместите на несколько дюймов ниже — либо обхватив петлю полотенца, гимнастическое кольцо или более низкую перекладину — так чтобы обе руки были заметно на разной высоте. | Повисните на полностью выпрямленных руках обеими руками, позволяя плечам опуститься естественным путем в пассивный вис. | Напрягите корпус, сожмите ягодицы и скрестите лодыжки, чтобы нижняя часть тела оставалась неподвижной на протяжении всего подхода. | Начните тягу, активно опуская и retracting лопатку на стороне с верхней рукой. | Двигайте верхний локоть вниз и назад, позволяя нижней руке помогать с уменьшенной силой. | Pull until your chin clears the bar or until the higher-side elbow reaches full flexion. | Под контролем опуститесь до полного выпрямления рук, сохраняя напряжение, а не пассивно роняйте вес. | Выполните все целевые повторения на одну сторону, затем поменяйте положение рук и выполните такое же количество повторений с противоположной стороны.
tHe: אחוז במוט משיכה ביד אחת בעמדת אחיזה מלמעלה רגילה והנח את היד השנייה כמה סנטימטרים נמוך יותר — באחיזת מגבת משוחללת, טבעת התעמלות או דרגה נמוכה — כך שהידיים בגבהים שונים באופן ניכר. | תלה בפשיטת זרועות מלאה בשתי הזרועות, ותן לכתפיים לצנוח באופן טבעי לתלייה פסיבית. | תכווץ את שרירי הליבה, כווץ את הישבנים, וחצה את הקרסולים כדי לשמור על הגוף התחתון יציב לכל אורך הסט. | Initiate the pull by actively depressing and retracting the shoulder blade on the higher-hand side. | דחף את המרפק העליון למטה ואחורה בזמן שאת מאפשר לזרוע התחתונה לסייע עם כוח מופחת. | Pull until your chin clears the bar or until the higher-side elbow reaches full flexion. | Lower yourself under control to full arm extension, maintaining tension rather than dropping passively. | בצע את כל חזרות היעד בצד אחד, ואז החלף את אופן האחיזה ובצע את אותו מספר חזרות בצד השני.

t: Stand or sit tall with your feet hip-width apart and your spine in a neutral position. | Extend both arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, interlacing your fingers with your palms facing away from you. | Tuck your chin gently toward your chest to lengthen the back of your neck. | Push your hands forward and allow your upper back to round, separating your shoulder blades as far apart as possible. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the muscles across your upper back to release. | On each exhale, try to deepen the reach slightly without forcing the stretch. | Slowly return to an upright position, unclasping your hands and letting your shoulder blades settle back together. | Repeat for 2–3 holds as needed.
tRu: Встаньте или сядьте прямо, поставив ноги на ширине бёдер и удерживая позвоночник в нейтральном положении. | Вытяните обе руки прямо перед собой на уровне плеч, переплетя пальцы и ладонями от себя. | Tuck your chin gently toward your chest to lengthen the back of your neck. | Push your hands forward and allow your upper back to round, separating your shoulder blades as far apart as possible. | Задержите положение на 20-30 секунд, дыша ровно и позволяя мышцам верхней части спины расслабляться. | На каждом выдохе попробуйте немного углубиться в растяжку, не форсируя ее. | Slowly return to an upright position, unclasping your hands and letting your shoulder blades settle back together. | Repeat for 2–3 holds as needed.
tHe: עמוד או שב זקוף עם רגליים ברוחב האגן ועמוד שדרה ניטרלי. | פשוט את שתי הידיים ישר קדימה בגובה הכתפיים, עם אצבעות משולבות וכפות ידיים פונות החוצה ממך. | Tuck your chin gently toward your chest to lengthen the back of your neck. | Push your hands forward and allow your upper back to round, separating your shoulder blades as far apart as possible. | Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and allowing the muscles across your upper back to release. | On each exhale, try to deepen the reach slightly without forcing the stretch. | Slowly return to an upright position, unclasping your hands and letting your shoulder blades settle back together. | Repeat for 2–3 holds as needed.

t: Stand between a set of parallel bars and grip each bar firmly with an overhand grip, palms facing inward. | Press through your palms to lift your body off the ground so your arms are fully extended and your torso hangs vertically. | Let your legs hang straight down with your feet together and your body in a neutral, upright position. | Brace your core and tilt your pelvis slightly posterior to engage the rectus abdominis before initiating the lift. | Keeping your legs as straight as possible, raise them in front of you by flexing at the hips until your thighs are parallel to the floor or higher. | Pause briefly at the top of the movement, maintaining tension in the abs and hip flexors. | Lower your legs slowly and under control back to the starting position without swinging or using momentum. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your upper body stable throughout each rep.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and core lightly braced. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and simultaneously drive your right knee up toward your chest as high as comfortable. | At the same time, swing your left arm forward and right arm back in a natural running-arm action. | Quickly lower your right foot back to the floor and immediately drive your left knee up, switching arms at the same time. | Continue alternating knees at a brisk, controlled pace, maintaining an upright posture throughout. | Keep your gaze forward, chest lifted, and avoid leaning backward as the pace increases. | Breathe rhythmically — exhale as each knee drives up, inhale as the foot returns to the floor. | Aim for a smooth, continuous rhythm for the desired duration or rep count before returning to a standing rest position.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your arms extended alongside your body or crossed over your chest. | Raise both legs until they are vertical, perpendicular to the floor, keeping them straight and feet together. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently toward the mat to stabilize your spine. | Exhale and curl your upper body upward, reaching your hands toward your feet while keeping your legs stationary. | Continue curling until your torso is as upright as your flexibility allows, pausing briefly at the top. | Inhale and slowly lower your upper body back to the mat under control, vertebra by vertebra. | Maintain the vertical leg position throughout each repetition and repeat for the desired number of reps.
tRu: Лягте на спину на коврик с вытянутыми руками вдоль тела или скрещёнными на груди. | Raise both legs until they are vertical, perpendicular to the floor, keeping them straight and feet together. | Напрягите корпус и мягко направьте поясницу к коврику, чтобы стабилизировать позвоночник. | Выдохните и поднимите верхнюю часть тела вверх, вытягивая руки к ногам, сохраняя ноги неподвижными. | Продолжайте сгибать, пока ваш корпус не станет максимально прямым, исходя из вашей гибкости, делая короткую паузу в верхней точке. | Выдохните и медленно опустите верхнюю часть тела обратно на мат под контролем, позвонок за позвонком. | Сохраняйте вертикальное положение ног на протяжении каждого повторения и повторите для желаемого количества повторений.

t: Step onto the vibration plate and set the frequency to a low-to-moderate level (25–40 Hz is a common starting range for stretching work). | Stand upright at the center of the plate with your feet hip-width apart, core lightly braced, and hands on your hips or at your sides for balance. | Step your right foot forward roughly two to three feet, placing it flat on the plate and keeping your left foot in place behind you. | Lower your back (left) knee toward the plate by bending both knees simultaneously, descending until your front thigh is roughly parallel to the plate and your rear knee hovers just above it. | Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking directly over your second toe — do not let it cave inward or drive past your toes. | Hold the lowered position for 2–3 seconds, allowing the vibration to work through your hips, thighs, and calves. | Push through your front heel to drive yourself back to the standing position. | Complete all reps on the right side, then switch legs and repeat the sequence with the left foot forward.

t: Set the vibration plate on the floor and select a low-to-moderate frequency to start, typically 20–30 Hz if adjustable. | Kneel behind the plate, place your hands shoulder-width apart on its surface, and wrap your fingers firmly around or flat against the plate edge to maintain control. | Step your feet back one at a time until your body forms a straight line from your heels to your head. | Stack your wrists directly under your shoulders and keep your arms fully extended without locking out aggressively. | Brace your core and squeeze your obliques to prevent your hips from sagging or piking upward. | Hold the position and breathe steadily — inhale through your nose, exhale through your mouth — without letting your shoulders shrug toward your ears. | Maintain the hold for the target duration, then step your feet forward one at a time, lower your knees to the floor, and remove your hands from the plate before the vibration stops.

t: Step onto the center of the vibration plate with your feet roughly hip-width apart and your weight distributed evenly across both feet. | Stand tall with a soft bend in your knees — do not lock them out — and keep your hips directly over your ankles. | Engage your core lightly to stabilize your spine, and allow your arms to rest at your sides or hold the support handles if the machine has them. | Set the plate to the desired frequency, typically between 25 and 40 Hz for general stretching and recovery, and turn it on. | Breathe steadily and remain relaxed from the hips down, letting the vibrations travel through your legs rather than actively resisting them. | Hold this standing position for the target duration, usually 30 to 60 seconds per set. | To finish, reduce the frequency or stop the plate before stepping off, then step down carefully onto stable ground.

t: Begin in a high plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart, wrists directly under your shoulders, body forming a straight line from head to heels. | Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your sides as you lower your body toward the floor in a slow, controlled descent — this is chaturanga dandasana. | Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, elbows at a 90-degree angle, and pause briefly without letting your hips sag or rise. | Press through your palms and roll over your toes to shift into upward-facing dog: straighten your arms, lift your chest, draw your shoulders back and down, and let only your hands and the tops of your feet contact the floor. | Hold the upward-facing dog position for one breath, keeping your thighs lifted off the floor and your neck long. | Exhale, tuck your toes, and press your hips up and back to transition into downward-facing dog, forming an inverted V-shape. | In downward-facing dog, straighten your arms, press your heels toward the floor, and lengthen your spine away from your hands. | Hold for one to three breaths before stepping or jumping your feet toward your hands to return to the top of the sequence or to a standing position.
tRu: Примите положение высокой планки: руки на ширине плеч, запястья точно под плечами, тело образует прямую линию от головы до пяток. | Напрягите корпус и держите локти близко к бокам, когда вы опускаете тело к полу в медленном и контролируемом опускании — это поза чатуранга дандасаны. | Опуститесь до тех пор, пока верхние руки не коснутся пола лёгким касанием, позволив полу обозначить нижнюю точку амплитуды. | Press through your palms and roll over your toes to shift into upward-facing dog: straighten your arms, lift your chest, draw your shoulders back and down, and let only your hands and the tops of your feet contact the floor. | Задержитесь в позе собаки мордой вверх на один вдох, держа бёдра поднятыми над полом и шею длинной. | Выдыхайте, поднимите пальцы ног и приподнимите бедра вверх и назад, чтобы перейти в позу downward-facing dog, образуя перевернутую V-образную форму. | В позе downward-facing dog выпрямите руки, направляйте пятки к полу и вытягивайте позвоночник от рук. | Удерживайте одно-три дыхания, затем шагните или прыгните ногами к рукам, чтобы вернуться в начало последовательности или в положение стоя.
tHe: התחל בפלאנק גבוה עם ידיים ברוחב הכתפיים, שורשי כף היד בדיוק מתחת לכתפיים, והגוף בקו ישר מהראש לעקבים. | הפעל את שרירי הליבה ושמור על מרפקיק קרובים לגופך כשאתה מוריד את גופך לכיוון הרצפה בירידה איטית ומבוקרת — זהו צ'טורנגה דנדאסנה. | Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor, elbows at a 90-degree angle, and pause briefly without letting your hips sag or rise. | Press through your palms and roll over your toes to shift into upward-facing dog: straighten your arms, lift your chest, draw your shoulders back and down, and let only your hands and the tops of your feet contact the floor. | Hold the upward-facing dog position for one breath, keeping your thighs lifted off the floor and your neck long. | שחרק, כנס אצבעות רגלייך, ודחוף את הירכיים שלך למעלה ואחורה כדי לעבור לתנוחת כלב פונה למטה, יוצר צורת V הפוכה. | In downward-facing dog, straighten your arms, press your heels toward the floor, and lengthen your spine away from your hands. | Hold for one to three breaths before stepping or jumping your feet toward your hands to return to the top of the sequence or to a standing position.

t: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, then lean back until your torso is at roughly a 45-degree angle to the ground. | Lift your feet off the floor so your shins are parallel to the ground, forming a V shape with your torso and thighs. | Bring both fists up to chin height in a guard position, keeping your elbows tucked close to your sides. | Brace your core and keep your lower back from rounding to maintain the V-sit hold throughout the set. | Rotate your torso to the right and extend your left arm across your body in a cross punch, twisting through your obliques. | Return your left fist to the guard position as you rotate back to center. | Rotate your torso to the left and throw a cross punch with your right arm, driving the rotation from your core. | Return to center and continue alternating punches for the desired number of repetitions. | Lower your feet to the floor in a controlled manner to complete the set.

t: Lie flat on your back with your legs fully extended and your arms stretched overhead, palms facing up. | Press your lower back gently toward the floor and brace your core before you begin. | In one controlled movement, raise both straight legs and your upper body at the same time, driving your hands forward toward your feet. | Continue lifting until your body forms a V shape, with your torso and legs meeting above your hips and your hands reaching toward your shins. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the rectus abdominis fully before lowering. | Lower your upper body and legs together in a slow, controlled descent back to the starting position. | Let your back and legs return fully to the floor before initiating the next repetition.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your legs extended and arms stretched overhead, holding the stability ball in both hands. | Press your lower back gently into the mat and engage your core before beginning the movement. | Exhale and simultaneously lift your arms (with the ball) and both legs off the floor, curling your torso and hips upward to form a V shape. | At the top of the movement, transfer the stability ball from your hands to your feet by squeezing it between your ankles. | Slowly lower both your arms and legs back toward the floor in a controlled descent, keeping the ball gripped between your feet. | Without allowing your legs or upper back to touch the floor completely, reverse the motion: raise both arms and legs again to form the V shape. | At the top, transfer the ball back from your feet to your hands. | Lower back down with control to complete one full repetition. | Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining a tight core and steady breathing throughout.

t: Step onto the treadmill and stand with feet on the side rails before starting the belt. | Set the speed to a comfortable walking pace — typically 2.5–4.0 mph — and step onto the moving belt. | Stand tall with your head up, eyes forward, and shoulders relaxed and slightly back. | Swing your arms naturally at your sides, bending them at roughly 90 degrees and alternating in sync with your opposite leg. | Strike the ground with your heel first, rolling through the midfoot and pushing off with your toes on each step. | Keep your core gently braced and your hips level throughout the stride — avoid excessive side-to-side swaying. | Breathe steadily and rhythmically; you should be able to hold a conversation without gasping. | If using an incline, increase the grade gradually (1–3%) to simulate outdoor terrain and increase intensity without raising speed. | When your session is complete, reduce the speed gradually, step to the side rails, and let the belt stop before stepping off.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, shoulders relaxed, and arms hanging at your sides. | Shift your weight onto your left foot and drive your right knee upward until your thigh is at least parallel to the floor. | At the same time, swing your left arm forward and your right arm back in a natural walking rhythm. | Lower your right foot back to the floor with control, landing softly through the ball of your foot. | Immediately shift your weight and drive your left knee up to the same height while swinging your right arm forward. | Continue alternating knees in a deliberate walking pace, maintaining an upright torso throughout. | Keep your gaze forward and your core lightly braced on every step to prevent your trunk from leaning backward. | Continue for the prescribed duration or distance, maintaining consistent knee height on each repetition.

t: Set the treadmill to its lowest speed (0.5–1.0 mph) before stepping on the belt. | Stand facing the rear of the treadmill and lightly grip both side rails for balance. | Step onto the moving belt and let it guide your feet into a smooth backward walking rhythm. | Once you feel stable, gradually increase the speed to a comfortable pace — typically 1.5–2.5 mph for most users. | Keep your torso upright and your core lightly braced; avoid leaning forward or hunching over the console. | Look straight ahead or slightly downward toward the belt — do not crane your neck to look behind you. | Take short, controlled steps, landing on the ball of your foot and rolling back through the toes to push off. | Maintain your grip on the rails whenever you feel unsteady, and release them gradually as your balance improves. | To finish, slow the belt back to its lowest speed, grip the rails firmly, and step off the sides of the treadmill — never jump off a moving belt.

t: Step onto the elliptical machine and grip the moving handlebars lightly with both hands, ensuring your feet are fully centered on the foot pedals. | Set the machine to your target resistance and incline level for VERSION 7 — a moderate resistance that challenges the legs without forcing you to lean heavily on the handles. | Begin pedaling forward in a smooth, fluid oval motion, allowing the machine to guide your stride rather than forcing a shortened or exaggerated range of motion. | Drive the handlebars with your arms in opposition to your legs — push forward with the right arm as the left leg drives forward — to engage the upper body and distribute the workload. | Maintain an upright posture with your chest lifted, shoulders relaxed away from your ears, and a slight engagement of your core throughout the session. | Keep your heels pressed into the foot pedals throughout the stride to maximize glute and hamstring activation and reduce excess pressure on the knees. | Monitor your pace and breathing, aiming for a conversational intensity — you should be able to speak in short sentences but feel your heart rate elevated. | Cool down during the final 3–5 minutes by gradually reducing speed and resistance before stepping off the machine. | Carefully step off the pedals only after the machine has come to a complete stop, holding the stationary handlebars for balance.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step forward with your right foot, planting it firmly and shifting your weight onto it. | As your weight transfers forward, swing your left leg up in front of you with the knee as straight as possible, aiming to kick to hip height or higher as your flexibility allows. | Simultaneously reach your right hand toward your left foot as the leg rises to encourage balance and add a gentle stretch through the back of the raised leg. | Lower your left leg and step it forward, then immediately kick your right leg up in the same controlled motion, reaching your left hand toward it. | Continue alternating sides and moving forward at a rhythmic, controlled pace — one step, one kick, opposite hand reach. | Keep your torso upright throughout; avoid leaning backward as the kicking leg rises. | Complete the desired distance or rep count, then decelerate to a controlled stop.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms at your sides. | Hinge at the hips and place both hands flat on the floor in front of your feet, bending your knees slightly if needed. | Walk your hands forward one at a time until your body forms a straight plank position with arms extended. | Once in the plank, press firmly through both palms and keep your core lightly braced. | Shift your hips straight back toward your heels while keeping your arms extended and your hands planted — you should feel a deep stretch along the sides of your torso and under your armpits. | Hold the stretched position for 2–3 seconds, breathing steadily. | Walk your hands back toward your feet step by step, returning to the hip-hinge position. | Stand back up to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of reps.

t: Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor about 30–45 cm from a wall, fingers spread wide and pointing forward. | Kick up into a handstand with your heels lightly resting against the wall, arms fully locked out and body vertical. | Squeeze your glutes, brace your core hard, and protract (push away) your shoulder blades to establish full body tension. | Tuck both knees toward your chest simultaneously, shifting your center of mass forward and away from the wall. | Begin leaning forward through your shoulders, letting your hips drop slowly by increasing the forward tilt of your torso. | Maintain straight, locked arms throughout — resist the descent using shoulder flexion strength and core tension, not by bending your elbows. | Lower your body as slowly as possible, aiming to hold the tucked horizontal position (tuck planche) for a beat before continuing. | Either hold the lowest position you can control for 1–3 seconds, or continue descending until your knees or feet touch the floor in a controlled manner. | Rest fully before the next repetition — this is a high-neurological-demand movement; 2–3 minutes between sets is appropriate.
tRu: Положите руки на ширине плеч на полу на расстоянии 30–45 см от стены, пальцы широко расставлены и направлены вперёд. | Поднимитесь в стойку на руками, чтобы пятки слегка касались стены, руки полностью выпрямлены, тело вертикально. | Squeeze your glutes, brace your core hard, and protract (push away) your shoulder blades to establish full body tension. | Tuck both knees toward your chest simultaneously, shifting your center of mass forward and away from the wall. | Начните наклоняться вперёд плечами, позволяя бёдрам медленно опускаться за счёт увеличения наклона корпуса вперёд. | Сохраняйте прямые, зафиксированные руки на протяжении всего движения — сопротивляйтесь опусканию с помощью силы сгибания плеч и напряжения корпуса, а не сгибая локти. | Опустите тело как можно медленнее, пытаясь удержать положение согнутой горизонтальной планки (уголок) на одну паузу, прежде чем продолжить. | Либо удерживайте самую нижнюю позицию, которую можете контролировать 1-3 секунды, либо продолжайте опускаться, пока колени или ступни не коснутся пола контролируемым образом. | Rest fully before the next repetition — this is a high-neurological-demand movement; 2–3 minutes between sets is appropriate.

t: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart and a target mark on the wall roughly 10 feet (3 m) high; hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and push your hips back to begin the squat descent. | Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and the ball at chest level. | Drive explosively through your heels to stand, extending your hips and knees simultaneously. | As you reach full hip extension, use the momentum to press and throw the medicine ball upward toward the target on the wall. | Watch the ball as it hits the target and rebounds off the wall. | Catch the ball with both hands at chest height, absorbing the impact by softening your elbows. | Immediately use the catch momentum to flow into the next squat descent without pausing. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps or time, maintaining a smooth, rhythmic squat-throw-catch cycle throughout.

tHe: Stand facing a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart and a target mark on the wall roughly 10 feet (3 m) high; hold a medicine ball at chest height with both hands. | הדק את הליבה, שמור על חזה גבוה ודחוף את האגן לאחור כדי להתחיל את ירידת הסקוואט. | Lower until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your knees tracking over your toes and the ball at chest level. | דחוף בכוח דרך עקבי הרגל כדי לעמוד, מתיחת הירכיים והברכיים בו זמנית. | בהגעה ליישור אגן מלא, השתמש במומנטום כדי ללחוץ ולזרוק את כדור התרופות מעלה לעבר המטרה על הקיר. | Watch the ball as it hits the target and rebounds off the wall. | תפוס את הכדור עם שתי הידיים בגובה החזה, סופק את ההשפעה על ידי הרפיית המרפקים. | Immediately use the catch momentum to flow into the next squat descent without pausing. | Repeat for the prescribed number of reps or time, maintaining a smooth, rhythmic squat-throw-catch cycle throughout.

nE: Wall Facing Single Leg Split Handstand Hold
nR: Стойка лицом к стене на одной ноге в шпагате
nH: החזקת עמידת ידיים מפושקת ברגל אחת מול קיר
t: Set up in a plank with your feet against the base of the wall and your palms flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart with fingers spread wide. | Walk your feet up the wall while stepping your hands back toward the baseboard until your palms are about 6–10 inches from it, your chest is close to the wall, and both legs are together. | Establish a solid base: lock out your elbows, press through your fingertips, push the floor away so your shoulders elevate and protract, and engage your core. | Slowly peel one leg off the wall and reach it away from the wall behind you while keeping the other leg in contact with the wall. | Press the wall leg straight up along the wall so it stays in line with your torso, and simultaneously reach the free leg as far back as your hip flexibility allows. | Square your hips as much as possible — avoid rotating the pelvis toward either leg; aim to keep both hip points level. | Hold the split position for the target duration, breathing steadily through your nose. | To exit, bring both legs back together against the wall, then walk your feet down or lower in a controlled tucked descent.

t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and raise one arm so it is roughly parallel to the floor. | Place your palm flat on the wall with your fingers pointing straight down toward the floor. | Straighten your elbow fully so your arm is extended but not locked with tension. | Slowly rotate your body away from the wall — turning your torso and shoulder away from your hand — until you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearm and wrist. | Keep your palm pressed firmly against the wall throughout; do not let the heel of your hand peel off. | Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily. | Release gently, shake out your wrist, then repeat on the opposite arm.

t: Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, roughly two to three feet from the base of the wall, with your fingers spread and wrists stacked under your shoulders. | Walk your feet up the wall behind you, one at a time, until your body forms a straight line from your hands to your heels — feet roughly hip-width apart on the wall. | Press firmly through both palms and lock your elbows without hyperextending them. | Brace your core by drawing your navel slightly toward your spine, and squeeze your glutes to prevent your hips from sagging toward the floor or piking upward. | Set your head in a neutral position, looking down at the floor between your hands so your neck stays in line with your spine. | Hold the position for the prescribed duration, breathing steadily — inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth — without letting tension drop. | To finish, walk your feet back down the wall one at a time and lower yourself in a controlled manner to the starting position.

nR: Жим у стены с касанием пяток
t: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and place both palms flat against it at roughly shoulder height and shoulder width apart. | Shift your weight onto your right foot, keeping a soft bend in the right knee. | Brace your core and keep your hips level — avoid tilting or rotating the pelvis. | Slowly extend your left leg straight back behind you, leading with the heel, until you feel a strong contraction in the left glute. | Pause briefly at the top of the range, then lower the foot under control until the heel lightly taps the floor. | Complete all reps on the left side, then switch to the right leg. | Throughout the set, keep your chest up and avoid arching the lower back to force extra range.
tRu: Stand facing a wall at arm's length and place both palms flat against it at roughly shoulder height and shoulder width apart. | Shift your weight onto your right foot, keeping a soft bend in the right knee. | Напрягите корпус и удерживайте бёдра на одном уровне — избегайте наклона или вращения таза. | Slowly extend your left leg straight back behind you, leading with the heel, until you feel a strong contraction in the left glute. | На мгновение остановитесь в верхней точке амплитуды, затем опустите стопу под контролем, пока пятка не коснется пола. | Выполните все повторения на левой стороне, затем поменяйте на правую ногу. | Throughout the set, keep your chest up and avoid arching the lower back to force extra range.

t: Stand facing a smooth wall, about one foot away, feet hip-width apart and core braced. | Place both palms flat on the wall at chest height, slightly narrower than shoulder-width, fingers pointing upward. | Lean your body weight gently into your hands so there is moderate pressure against the wall. | Bend your elbows slightly — about 20 to 30 degrees — so the triceps are already under light tension. | Without moving your shoulders or body, press your palms firmly into the wall to straighten your elbows, contracting the triceps brachii at the end of the movement. | Immediately release just enough to return to the slightly bent starting position — this short, controlled return is the 'pulse.' | Repeat the press-and-release in a steady, rhythmic tempo, keeping the range of motion small and intentional throughout each rep. | Keep your back flat, hips neutral, and avoid shrugging your shoulders toward your ears. | Complete the target reps, then step back from the wall and relax your arms.

t: Place a weight plate or low step against the wall and stand with your back flat against the wall, heels on the elevated surface and toes pointing slightly outward. | Walk your feet forward until your shins are roughly vertical or your knees are just slightly in front of your ankles. | Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor (or as close as your mobility allows), forming a 90° angle at the hips and knees. | Press your entire back — lower back included — firmly into the wall and keep your head neutral. | Distribute your weight evenly through the full foot, letting the heel elevation naturally shift load toward the quads and glutes. | Brace your core, squeeze your glutes lightly, and hold the position for the target duration while breathing steadily. | To finish, press through your heels and walk your feet back toward the wall to stand upright.

t: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall, feet together or no more than a few inches apart and roughly 12–18 inches out from the wall. | Slide your back down the wall until your hips and knees are at approximately a 90-degree angle and your thighs are parallel to the floor. | Check that your knees are directly over your ankles, not caving inward or drifting past your toes. | Press your entire back, from your lower back to your upper back, firmly into the wall throughout the hold. | Keep your arms either extended in front of you or resting lightly on your thighs — do not use them to push off your knees. | Hold the position for the target duration, breathing steadily and keeping your core braced. | To finish, push through your heels and slide back up the wall to a standing position.

t: Start in a push-up position with your heels against the base of a wall, arms fully extended, hands shoulder-width apart, and core braced. | Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your body forms a rigid plank — this position is your base for the entire movement. | Begin walking your feet up the wall one step at a time, simultaneously walking your hands backward toward the wall to keep your body aligned. | Continue the coordinated hand-and-foot walk until your chest is as close to the wall as your current strength and mobility allow, ideally within a fist's distance. | Hold the near-vertical position for a breath, pressing firmly through your hands and maintaining full-body tension. | Reverse the movement by stepping your feet down the wall and walking your hands away from the wall at the same pace. | Continue until you return to the starting push-up position with your heels back at the wall's base. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the target number of reps.

tHe: Start in a push-up position with your heels against the base of a wall, arms fully extended, hands shoulder-width apart, and core braced. | Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your body forms a rigid plank — this position is your base for the entire movement. | התחל לטפס עם הרגליים על הקיר צעד אחר צעד, תוך צעידת הידיים לאחור לכיוון הקיר כדי לשמור על גוף מיושר. | המשך את ההליכה המתואמת בידיים וברגליים עד שהחזה שלך קרוב ככל האפשר לקיר, בהתאם לכוח והגמישות הנוכחיים שלך, באופן אידיאלי במרחק אגודל. | Hold the near-vertical position for a breath, pressing firmly through your hands and maintaining full-body tension. | Reverse the movement by stepping your feet down the wall and walking your hands away from the wall at the same pace. | המשך עד שאתה חוזר למצב ההתחלתי של השכיבות עם עקביך חזרו לבסיס הקיר. | Rest briefly, then repeat for the target number of reps.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides, and core lightly braced. | Step your right foot forward into a forward lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor until both legs reach roughly 90 degrees; hold for one breath, then return to standing. | Step forward again into a lunge and add a torso rotation toward the lead knee, extending both arms to the side to open the thoracic spine; return to standing. | Lunge forward a third time and reach both arms overhead and slightly back to open the hip flexors and extend the lumbar spine; hold for one breath, then return to standing. | Step your right foot out wide to the side into a lateral lunge, pushing the hips back and keeping the opposite leg straight to stretch the inner thigh and groin; return to standing. | Step your right foot behind you into a reverse lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor to stretch the front of the hip; hold for one breath, then push through the front heel to stand. | Repeat the entire five-move sequence on the left leg, matching the same order of movements. | Complete 2–3 full rounds per side, moving at a controlled, rhythmic pace throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core lightly braced and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a forward lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor until both knees form roughly 90-degree angles. t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, core lightly braced, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward roughly two to three feet and lower your body until your right thigh is approximately parallel to the floor and your left knee hovers just above the ground. | Ensure your right knee tracks directly over your right foot and does not cave inward or push past your toes. | Keep your torso upright and your hips squared forward — avoid rotating toward the lead leg. | From this lunge position, raise both arms straight overhead, pressing your palms together or keeping them shoulder-width apart, to stretch the upper arms, shoulders, and back. | Hold the end position for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily and sinking slightly deeper into the lunge on each exhale to increase the hip-flexor stretch. | Lower your arms, push through your right heel, and return to the starting standing position. | Repeat the movement on the same side for the desired number of holds before switching legs, or switch sides each set as directed.

t: Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor and keeping your right shin vertical. | Place both hands flat on the floor on either side of your right foot to establish your base position. | Rotate your right arm up toward the ceiling, opening your chest and turning through your upper back — hold briefly, then return your hand to the floor. | Bring your right elbow down toward the inside of your right foot, deepening the hip flexor and inner-thigh stretch — hold briefly. | Press your right hand into the floor and reach your left arm straight overhead, creating a lateral lean through your waist — hold briefly. | Place both hands back on the floor, then shift your hips back to straighten your right leg and stretch the right hamstring — hold briefly. | Return to the deep lunge position and raise both arms overhead, reaching up to open the shoulders and extend the thoracic spine — hold briefly. | Lower your arms and rotate your torso to the right, extending your right arm behind you at shoulder height to stretch the back and waist — hold briefly. | Return to the starting position, then switch legs and repeat the full seven-position sequence on the left side. | Complete the desired number of rounds on each side before moving into your main training session.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor until both knees are bent at roughly 90°. Keep your torso upright. This is your base position for all six moves. | Position 1 — Hip sink: Press your hips gently downward to open the front of the left hip. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 2 — Thoracic rotation: Place both hands on your right thigh and rotate your torso to the right, reaching your right arm overhead toward the ceiling. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 3 — Side reach: Return to center and extend your left arm up and over to the right, stretching the left side of your waist. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 4 — Elbow drop: Lower your right elbow to the floor inside your right foot, opening the hip further. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 5 — Hamstring shift: Straighten your right leg and hinge your hips back with a flat back to stretch the back of the right thigh. Hold 2–3 seconds. | Position 6 — Rotation return: Rebend the right knee, rotate your torso back to center, and push through your right foot to return to standing. | Repeat the full six-position flow on the left side, stepping the left foot forward.

t: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, core lightly braced, and arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a deep lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor while keeping your right knee stacked directly over your right ankle. | Place both hands on the floor inside your right foot for stability. | Rotate your torso to the right, lifting your right arm toward the ceiling and opening your chest to the side — hold for one to two seconds. | Return your right hand to the floor, then extend your right arm forward and your left arm back, creating a T-shape with your upper body to stretch the shoulders and waist. | From there, reach both arms overhead, interlacing your fingers or pressing palms together, and gently side-bend to the left to stretch the right hip flexor and waist. | Hold the end position for two to three seconds, feeling a full stretch through the chest, shoulder, thigh, and hip. | Return to the starting standing position and repeat the entire sequence on the opposite side, stepping the left foot forward. | Complete two to three controlled repetitions per side before your main workout.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides. | Step your right foot forward into a lunge, lowering your left knee toward the floor until both knees are bent at roughly 90 degrees. | Keep your front shin vertical and your torso upright, with your core lightly braced. | Reach both arms overhead or extend them out to the sides to lengthen the waist and open the hips further. | Hold the stretched position for two to three seconds, breathing steadily. | Return your arms to a neutral position and push through your front heel to stand back up. | Repeat the lunge on the opposite leg, stepping the left foot forward and performing the same reach. | Alternate legs for the prescribed number of repetitions on each side, moving with control throughout.

t: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your weight evenly distributed. Take a breath in to prepare. | Shift your weight onto your right foot, pressing all four corners of the foot firmly into the floor. | On an exhale, hinge forward at the hip and simultaneously lift your left leg behind you, keeping both hips squared toward the floor. | Continue lowering your torso and raising your left leg until both are roughly parallel to the floor, forming a straight line from your raised heel to the crown of your head. | Extend your arms forward alongside your ears, palms facing each other, or reach them back alongside your torso — choose the position that best supports your balance. | Fix your gaze on a still point on the floor about one metre ahead of your standing foot to anchor your balance. | Hold the position for 5–10 slow breaths, keeping your standing knee soft rather than locked, your core braced, and your raised foot flexed. | To exit, exhale and slowly lower the lifted leg back to the floor, stepping both feet together before switching sides. | Repeat on the left leg, holding for the same duration.
tRu: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your weight evenly distributed. t: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, toes turned out 10–20°. | Hold a dumbbell, plate, or similar weight at chest height with both hands and extend your arms forward so the weight acts as a counterbalance. | Brace your core, lift your chest, and take a deep breath in before you begin the descent. | Initiate the squat by pushing your knees out in line with your toes and sitting your hips back and down, keeping your torso as upright as possible. | Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, or as deep as your mobility allows while keeping your heels flat on the ground. | Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your entire foot to extend your hips and knees simultaneously back to standing. | Exhale at the top of the rep, reset your brace, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Select a weight plate or dumbbell and sit on the center of a stability ball, feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. | Walk your feet forward until your lower back is supported by the ball and your torso is parallel to the floor — the ball should sit in the curve of your lumbar spine. | Hold the weight at your chest with both hands, or extend your arms and hold it behind your head for a longer lever. | Brace your core and plant your feet firmly so the ball stays stable throughout the set. | Exhale and curl your upper body upward by contracting your rectus abdominis, lifting your shoulder blades away from the ball until your torso is roughly 30–45 degrees above horizontal. | Hold the top position for one count, squeezing your abs without pulling on your neck or jerking the weight. | Inhale and slowly lower your upper body back down, allowing your abs to stretch over the ball before beginning the next repetition. | Complete all reps, then lower the weight to your chest before carefully sitting upright off the ball.

t: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart. | Hold a weight plate or dumbbell with both hands and extend your arms straight overhead, keeping them close to your ears — they stay in this extended position for the entire set. | Brace your core and press your lower back gently into the mat to establish a stable starting position. | Exhale and curl your shoulders and upper back off the floor, leading with your chest — not your chin — while keeping your arms fully extended and the weight reaching toward the ceiling. | Continue curling until your shoulder blades are fully off the floor and you feel maximum contraction in your rectus abdominis. | Hold the top position for one count, squeezing your abs hard. | Inhale and slowly lower your upper back back to the floor under control, resisting the pull of the weight throughout the descent. | Reset your core brace before beginning the next rep.

t: Lie flat on your back with your low back pressed firmly into the floor — there should be no gap between your spine and the mat. | Hold a dumbbell or weight plate in both hands and press your arms straight up toward the ceiling, directly above your shoulders. | Raise both legs so your hips and knees are bent to 90°, shins parallel to the floor — this is your starting position. | Take a deep breath in, then exhale fully and brace your core by drawing your ribs down and pressing your low back hard into the floor. | While maintaining that brace, slowly lower your right arm overhead toward the floor and simultaneously extend your left leg toward the floor, stopping just before either touches. | Pause for one second at the bottom, keeping your low back completely flat. | Reverse the movement under control, returning your arm and leg to the starting position. | Without losing tension, repeat on the opposite side — left arm down, right leg out — to complete one full rep. | Continue alternating sides for the target number of reps, re-bracing before each rep.

t: Lie flat on a bench or the floor with your legs extended and your arms at your sides, gripping the edges of the bench or pressing your palms lightly against the floor for stability. | Clamp a light dumbbell securely between your feet or ankles, holding it in place by squeezing your feet together. | Brace your core and press your lower back into the bench or floor to establish a stable starting position. | Keeping your feet together and the dumbbell controlled, bend your knees and draw them toward your chest in a smooth arc. | Raise your knees until your thighs are at or just past a 90-degree angle with your torso, or until your hips are fully flexed. | Pause briefly at the top, maintaining core tension and keeping the dumbbell from shifting. | Lower your legs in a controlled manner back to the starting position, resisting the weight on the way down rather than letting it drop. | Complete all reps without allowing your lower back to arch excessively or your feet to unclasp the dumbbell.

nR: Присед у стены на фитболе с весом

t: Place an exercise ball between your lower back and a smooth wall, positioning it at the curve of your lumbar spine. | Step your feet forward 12–18 inches from the wall, hip-width apart, toes turned out slightly. | Hold a dumbbell or weight plate at your chest, or secure a weighted vest before starting. | Brace your core, keep your chest tall, and begin to squat by bending your knees and letting your hips travel straight down the wall. | Lower yourself until your thighs are parallel to the floor (or as low as is comfortable), letting the ball roll up your back naturally. | Keep your knees tracking over your second toe and avoid letting them cave inward. | Pause briefly at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position. | Squeeze your glutes at the top without hyperextending your lower back. | Complete all reps, then step your feet back toward the wall, stand tall, and set the weight down before stepping away from the ball.

t: Attach a weight plate to a dip belt, put on a weighted vest, or grip a dumbbell between your feet before approaching the dip cage. | Take hold of the dip cage's parallel vertical handles with a neutral grip — palms facing each other — and hands roughly shoulder-width apart. | Hang at full arm extension, allowing your shoulder blades to elevate so your lats get a full stretch at the bottom. | Depress your shoulder blades downward and back before bending your elbows, engaging your lats from the start of each rep. | Pull your chest toward the handles by driving your elbows straight down toward your hips, keeping your torso upright or with a slight rearward lean. | Continue pulling until your chin clears the level of the handles, then pause briefly and squeeze your lats and upper back. | Lower yourself under control over 2–3 seconds back to a full hang, letting your shoulder blades re-elevate at the bottom to restore the full range of motion. | Complete all your reps, then step or drop down from the cage safely.

t: Attach your extra weight securely before approaching the bar: clip a dip belt around your hips, don a weighted vest, or place a dumbbell between your feet. | Grip the pull-up bar with a supinated (underhand, palms facing you) grip, hands roughly shoulder-width apart or slightly narrower. | Hang at full arm extension — a dead hang — with your shoulders relaxed and your core lightly braced. | Depress and retract your shoulder blades to engage your lats, then initiate the pull by driving your elbows down and back toward your hips. | Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it or your upper chest lightly touches the bar, keeping your elbows tracking close to your torso. | Pause briefly at the top, squeezing your lats and biceps. | Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang over 2–3 seconds, resisting the urge to drop quickly. | Complete all reps, then carefully dismount and detach the added weight before stepping away from the bar.
tRu: Надёжно закрепите дополнительное отягощение перед подходом к перекладине: пристегните пояс с весом на бёдра, наденьте жилет с отягощением или зажмите гантель между стопами. | Возьмитесь за перекладину для подтягиваний supinated (хват снизу, ладонями к вам) хватом, руки на расстоянии примерно ширины плеч или уже. | Повисните на полностью выпрямленных руках — вис на прямых руках — с расслабленными плечами и легким напряжением корпуса. | Опустите и retract лопатки, чтобы напрячь широчайшие мышцы, затем начните тягу, двигая локти вниз и назад к бедрам. | Pull your chest toward the bar until your chin clears it or your upper chest lightly touches the bar, keeping your elbows tracking close to your torso. | Задержитесь на мгновение в верхней точке, сжимая широчайшие мышцы спины и бицепс. | Под контролем вернитесь в полный вис на прямых руках в течение 2–3 секунд, сопротивляясь желанию быстро опуститься. | Выполните все повторения, затем осторожно сойдите и снимите дополнительный вес, прежде чем отойти от штанги.

t: Sit on the floor with your upper back resting against the long edge of a flat bench, knees bent and feet flat on the floor about hip-width apart. | Roll a barbell (or place a weight plate) over your hips, positioning it just below your hip bones. t: Set the hyperextension bench so the top pad rests just below your hip bones, leaving your hips free to hinge. t: Set an adjustable bench to a 30–45 degree incline and sit back against it with your feet flat on the floor. | Hold two weight plates sandwiched together at chest height, pressing your palms firmly into each side of the plates to create constant inward pressure. | Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades slightly against the pad. | Begin with the plates at mid-chest level, arms bent and elbows pointing outward at roughly 45 degrees. | Press the plates upward and forward along the incline angle, fully extending your arms while maintaining the squeeze between your palms. | Hold the fully extended position for one count, feeling the contraction in the upper chest. | Slowly return the plates back toward your chest under control, keeping the inward squeeze throughout the entire range of motion. | Repeat for the desired number of repetitions without releasing the lateral pressure between palms.

t: Put on a weighted vest, or have a training partner ready with a weight plate, then set a barbell in a rack (or use a Smith machine bar) at roughly hip height. | Lie underneath the bar so it sits directly above your chest when your arms are fully extended upward. | Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand (pronated) grip, thumbs wrapped fully around the bar. t: Lie flat on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your core before you pick up the kettlebell. | Hold the kettlebell in one hand and press it straight toward the ceiling, arm fully extended, wrist stacked over your elbow over your shoulder. | Raise both legs so your hips and knees are at 90°, shins parallel to the floor. This is your starting position. | Inhale to prepare, then exhale and slowly lower the leg opposite your kettlebell arm, extending it toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed flat. | Lower the leg until it hovers a few inches above the floor — or as low as you can without your back arching off the ground. | Pause for one beat at the bottom, maintaining a rigid torso and keeping the kettlebell locked directly overhead. | Exhale and draw the leg back up to the 90° starting position with control, completing one rep. | Complete all reps on one side, then switch the kettlebell to the other hand and repeat with the opposite leg.

t: Sit upright on a stability ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest. | Walk your feet forward and lean back until your mid-to-lower back rests on the ball, with your knees bent at roughly 90 degrees. | Brace your core and tuck your chin slightly toward your chest — maintain this neutral head position throughout the set. | Curl your upper body upward into a crunch by contracting the rectus abdominis, lifting your shoulder blades off the ball. | As you begin the crunch, simultaneously extend both legs forward until they are nearly straight and parallel to the floor. | Hold the top position for one count, feeling the contraction in your abdominals and the tension through your hip flexors. | Slowly reverse the movement — bend your knees back to 90 degrees and lower your upper body back onto the ball under control. | Recheck your position on the ball as needed, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

t: Lie on your side on a mat with your body in a straight line, hips stacked directly on top of each other. | Place a weight plate or ankle weight on the outside of your top thigh, just above the knee, and hold it in place with your top hand. | Rest your bottom arm on the floor and use it to support your head, or extend it along the floor for balance. | Keep your bottom leg slightly bent for stability and your top leg straight with toes pointing forward. | Brace your core to prevent your hips from rolling forward or backward during the movement. | Exhale and lift your top leg upward until it reaches approximately 45 degrees, leading with the outer heel rather than the toes. | Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the gluteus medius. | Inhale and lower your leg back to the starting position in a controlled manner without letting it drop or rest on the bottom leg. | Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other.
tRu: Лягте на бок на мате, тело вытянуто в прямую линию, таз расположен непосредственно один над другим. | Положите weight plate or ankle weight снаружи вашего top бедра, чуть выше колена, и hold it in place с вашей top рукой. | Rest your bottom arm on the floor and use it to support your head, or extend it along the floor for balance. | Держите нижнюю ногу слегка согнутой для стабильности и верхнюю ногу прямой, с носками, направленными вперёд. | Напрягите пресс, не давая бёдрам заваливаться вперёд или назад во время движения. | Выдыхайте и поднимайте верхнюю ногу вверх до угла примерно 45 градусов, ведя наружным краем стопы, а не пальцами. | Пауза в верхней точке и сжатие средней ягодичной мышцы. | Выдохните и опустите ногу обратно в исходное положение в контролируемом режиме, не давая ей упасть или лечь на нижнюю ногу. | Выполните все повторения на одну сторону, затем перейдите на другую.

t: Place a folded towel at the edge of a flat bench and lie face-down with your upper chest at the edge, so your head and neck extend past the end and can move freely. | Hold a weight plate behind your head, cupping it in both hands against the back of your skull. | Let your head drop toward the floor under control until you feel a comfortable stretch through the back of the neck — this is your starting position. | Keeping your torso and chest pressed flat on the bench, extend your head upward by contracting the muscles at the back of your neck. | Raise your head until it is in line with your spine or slightly above — do not hyperextend beyond a neutral position. | Pause briefly at the top, maintaining tension in the neck muscles. | Lower your head slowly back to the starting position over 2–3 seconds, resisting the weight on the way down. | Complete all reps, then remove the weight plate before sitting up.
tRu: Положите сложенное полотенце на край плоской скамьи и лягте на живот с верхней частью груди на краю, чтобы ваша голова и шея выступали за конец и могли свободно двигаться. | Держите весовой диск у груди одной рукой и легко держитесь за стойку стойки или другой прочный опору для равновесия другой рукой. | Позвольте вашей голове опуститься под контролем к полу, пока вы не почувствуете комфортную растяжку в задней части шеи — это ваше исходное положение. | Держа туловище и грудь прижатыми к скамье, поднимите голову вверх, напрягая мышцы задней поверхности шеи. | Raise your head until it is in line with your spine or slightly above — do not hyperextend beyond a neutral position. | На вершине движения сделайте короткую паузу, сохраняя напряжение в шейных мышцах. | Медленно опустите голову обратно в исходное положение за 2–3 секунды, сопротивляясь весу на пути вниз. | Выполните все повторения, затем снимите весовой диск, прежде чем сесть.

nE: Weighted Lying Neck Extension (with head harness)
nR: Разгибания шеи лёжа с весом (с упряжью)
nH: פשיטות צוואר בשכיבה עם משקל (עם רתמת ראש)
t: Select a very light weight plate to start — even experienced lifters should begin with 2.5–5 lb until the movement pattern is well established. | Sit on the end of a flat bench, then carefully lie back so the back of your head hangs just off the edge; your shoulders should remain fully supported on the bench. | Fit the head harness snugly over your skull and attach the chain or strap to your loaded weight plate, allowing the plate to hang toward the floor. | Let the weight pull your head into full flexion — chin moving toward your chest — so you reach a comfortable starting stretch at the bottom of the range of motion. | Brace your core lightly and keep your shoulders pressed flat against the bench throughout the set. | Using only your neck extensors, slowly lift your head by pushing the back of your skull upward and backward, extending the neck until your head is roughly level with or just above the bench surface. | Pause briefly at the top, consciously squeezing the posterior neck musculature. | Lower your head back down in a slow, controlled manner — take at least 2–3 seconds on the descent — returning to the stretched starting position. | Complete the desired number of reps, then carefully remove the harness and sit up slowly before standing.

t: Lie face-up on a flat bench with your head and neck hanging off the edge, unsupported. | Place a folded towel between the weight plate and your forehead for padding, then hold the plate in position with both hands. | Begin with your head slightly extended below bench level — this is your starting position. | Tuck your chin and slowly curl your head upward, flexing the neck until your chin is as close to your chest as comfortable. | Pause briefly at the top, feeling the sternocleidomastoid fully contracted. | Lower your head back down under control to the starting position, resisting the weight on the way down. | Complete all reps, then use both hands to carefully remove the weight before sitting up.

nE: Weighted Lying Neck Flexion (with head harness)
nR: Сгибания шеи лёжа с весом (с упряжью)
nH: כפיפות צוואר בשכיבה עם משקל (עם רתמת ראש)
t: Attach the head harness securely, ensuring the straps are snug and the weight hook sits at the front of your head. | Clip a light weight plate to the harness chain, starting conservatively — most people begin with 2.5–5 kg (5–10 lb) or even an empty harness. | Lie face-up on a flat bench so that your head hangs off the end, with your neck in a neutral or slightly extended position. | Place your hands on your chest or grip the sides of the bench for stability. | Slowly lower your chin toward your chest, flexing the neck through a full, controlled range of motion. | Pause briefly at the top of the movement with the neck fully flexed. | Lower your head back to the start position under control, allowing a gentle stretch at the bottom. | Complete all reps without jerking or using momentum, then unclip the weight before removing the harness.
tRu: Надёжно закрепите головной ремень, убедившись, что лямки плотно сидят, а крюк для веса находится спереди головы. | Прицепите к цепи жилетного ремня лёгкий диск, начиная с консервативного варианта — большинство людей начинают с 2,5–5 кг (5–10 фунтов) или даже с пустого жилета. | Лягте на спину на горизонтальную скамью так, чтобы голова свисала с края, шея в нейтральном или слегка выгнутом положении. | Положите руки на грудь или держитесь за стороны скамьи для стабильности. | Slowly lower your chin toward your chest, flexing the neck through a full, controlled range of motion. | Пауза в верхней точке движения с полным сгибанием шеи. | Опустите голову обратно в исходное положение под контролем, позволяя мягкой растяжке в нижней точке. | Выполните все повторения без рывков и использования инерции, затем отсоедините вес перед снятием жгута.
tHe: חבר את רתמת הראש היטב, תוך הקפדה שהרצועות מהודקות וו המשקל יושב בקדמת הראש. | חבר לוח משקל קל לשרשרת האביזר, התחל בצורה שמרנית — רוב האנשים מתחילים עם 2.5–5 ק״ג (5–10 ליברות) או אפילו עם אביזר ריק. | Lie face-up on a flat bench so that your head hangs off the end, with your neck in a neutral or slightly extended position. | Place your hands on your chest or grip the sides of the bench for stability. | Slowly lower your chin toward your chest, flexing the neck through a full, controlled range of motion. | Pause briefly at the top of the movement with the neck fully flexed. | Lower your head back to the start position under control, allowing a gentle stretch at the bottom. | בצע את כל החזרות מבל להשתמש בתנופה או בתנועה חדה, ואף פעם לא לשחרר את המשקל לפני הסרת האביזר.

t: Lie flat on your back on a bench or the floor with your head extended just off the edge so it can rotate freely. | Hold a light weight plate flat against one side of your head, using both hands to keep it stable. | Begin with your head turned toward the side holding the weight, so the weight is on top. | Slowly rotate your head away from the weight, turning as far as comfortable range of motion allows, letting the plate provide resistance throughout the movement. | Pause briefly at the end range without straining, then slowly rotate back to the starting position under control. | Complete all reps on one side, then reposition the weight plate to the opposite side of your head and repeat. | Keep your shoulders flat and relaxed against the surface throughout the entire set. | Lower the weight and rest briefly between sides to avoid excessive fatigue on the neck rotators.
tRu: Лягте на спину на скамью или на пол, голова немного свисает с края, чтобы она могла свободно вращаться. | Держите лёгкий весовой диск плоско с одной стороны головы, используя обе руки для удержания. | Начните с повёрнутой головой в сторону удерживаемого отягощения, чтобы отягощение оказалось сверху. | Slowly rotate your head away from the weight, turning as far as comfortable range of motion allows, letting the plate provide resistance throughout the movement. | На мгновение остановитесь в конечной точке амплитуды, не напрягаясь, затем медленно вернитесь в исходное положение под контролем. | Выполните все повторения на одну сторону, затем перенесите весовую пластину на противоположную сторону головы и повторите. | Держите плечи плоскими и расслабленными на поверхности на протяжении всего подхода. | Опустите вес и сделайте короткую паузу между сторонами, чтобы избежать чрезмерной усталости вращателей шеи.

nE: Weighted Lying Neck Side to Side
nR: Наклоны шеи из стороны в сторону лёжа с весом
nH: הטיות צוואר מצד לצד בשכיבה עם משקל
t: Lie face-up on a flat bench with your head extended just beyond the edge so it hangs freely; keep your shoulders flat and your spine neutral. | Place a small weight plate (2.5–5 lb) on the side of your head just above the temple, or attach a weighted head harness and adjust it to sit comfortably. | Support the weight lightly with one hand to prevent it from sliding during the first few reps. | Begin with your head in a neutral position — ears aligned over shoulders, chin neither tucked nor raised. | Slowly tilt your head toward the weighted side, allowing gravity and the weight to guide a controlled lateral flexion until you feel a mild stretch on the opposite side. | Pause briefly at the end range, then contract the muscles on the weighted side to bring your head back to neutral. | Without stopping, continue in one fluid arc to the opposite side, tilting your head away from where the weight now rests. | Return to neutral to complete one full side-to-side repetition. | Complete all reps, then carefully remove the weight before sitting up slowly to avoid dizziness.
tRu: Лягте на спину на горизонтальную скамью так, чтобы голова выступала за край и свободно свисала; держите плечи прижатыми, позвоночник в нейтральном положении. | Положите небольшой весовой диск (2.5–5 lb) с стороны головы чуть выше виска или наденьте weighted head harness и отрегулируйте его для комфортного положения. | Support the weight lightly with one hand to prevent it from sliding during the first few reps. | Начните с нейтрального положения головы — уши над плечами, подбородок ни прижат, ни поднят. | Slowly tilt your head toward the weighted side, allowing gravity and the weight to guide a controlled lateral flexion until you feel a mild stretch on the opposite side. | На мгновение остановитесь в конечной точке амплитуды, затем сожмите мышцы на стороне с весом, чтобы вернуть голову в нейтральное положение. | Without stopping, continue in one fluid arc to the opposite side, tilting your head away from where the weight now rests. | Return to neutral to complete one full side-to-side repetition. | Выполните все повторения, затем осторожно снимите вес перед тем, как медленно садиться, чтобы избежать головокружения.
